title: Shared-level and leaderboard traffic uses unauthenticated HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/get_level.php";
	public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/get_highscore.php";
entry_point: Traffic to the four HTTP endpoints declared in ApoClockConstants.java:5-9 becomes attacker-controlled when the apo-games.de server is malicious or an attacker controls DNS/routing on the victim's network.
sink: Raw URLConnection streams send and receive level data at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:121-140 and 162-204, and score data at ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:81-103 and 125-155.
data_path: Startup reaches ApoClockPanel.init() at ApoClockPanel.java:95-98, then loadUserlevels() at lines 139-146, ApoClockUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at ApoClockUserlevels.java:22-32, and ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.load(). Entering Arcade starts ApoClockHighscore.loadHighscore() through ApoClockArcarde.java:37-45. Editor uploads follow ApoClockEditor.java:166-183 to ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.save(); score submissions follow ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89 to ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save().
attack_scenario: An attacker on the victim's Wi-Fi intercepts the initial cleartext request. They can replace downloaded leaderboard entries, modify an outgoing score, or return a crafted shared-level record. The last option reaches the game parser described in ApoClock-02 and can hang the victim's game.
preconditions: The device reports an active network at ApoClock.java:36-48, the Android build permits cleartext HTTP, and the attacker controls the server or the network path.
validation_plan: Run the app or an emulator through an HTTP interception proxy. Launch the app and enter Arcade to observe plaintext requests for get_level.php and get_highscore.php; complete/upload a level and finish an Arcade game to observe the plaintext POSTs. Rewrite one response or POST parameter and confirm that the client consumes or sends the modified value without any TLS or authenticity failure.

title: Downloaded level can set a zero clock interval and hang the update loop
entry_point: The first line of every 11-line record returned by get_level.php is accepted as an untrusted level string at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:179-204.
sink: The parsed velocity is stored without validation by ApoClockEntityClock.java:17-20. ApoClockPuzzleGame.think() uses it as the threshold at line 226 and subtracts it at line 238; a value of zero makes the while loop permanently true without changing curTime.
data_path: ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.load() adds the response line at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-184; ApoClockUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() copies it at ApoClockUserlevels.java:44-54; Puzzle's userlevels button calls setPuzzleGame() at ApoClockPuzzle.java:63-66; ApoClockPanel.java:234-248 calls ApoClockPuzzleGame.loadLevel(); and ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:134-153 parses the five fields into an ApoClockEntityClock.
attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP interceptor supplies a syntactically complete record whose level line is "240,260,40,0,0" and whose remaining ten metadata lines contain valid numbers/text. The victim opens Puzzle, selects userlevels, and taps to start. The next update enters the loop at ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:226 and never exits, producing an ANR or requiring the game to be killed.
preconditions: The crafted record must be downloaded successfully, the victim must select the shared level and tap to start it, and cleartext level traffic must be permitted. A malicious uploader can use the same route if save_level.php stores arbitrary submitted level strings; the client upload contains only the URL-encoded level at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:121-133, but server-side validation was not available to verify.
validation_plan: Use an HTTP proxy to answer get_level.php with eleven lines: level "240,260,40,0,0", then valid values such as time 1, count 1, total 1, name x, four zero ratings, id 1, and current time 0. Launch the app, enter Puzzle > userlevels, select the level, and tap outside the navigation controls. Capture a thread dump or ANR trace showing the update thread repeating ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:226-238.

title: Automatic level download consumes an unbounded response
entry_point: A malicious get_level.php server or HTTP interceptor controls the entire response read from the URLConnection opened at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:162-179.
sink: The loop at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207 has no byte, line-length, record-count, or time bound and retains response fields in multiple ArrayLists. Afterward, ApoClockUserlevels.sortByUpload() performs a nested insertion sort at ApoClockUserlevels.java:57-74.
data_path: ApoClockPanel.init() automatically invokes loadUserlevels() at ApoClockPanel.java:95-98; its thread calls ApoClockUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at ApoClockPanel.java:139-146 and ApoClockUserlevels.java:22-28; load() then reads until attacker-controlled EOF. The same unbounded read pattern is repeated for user-triggered leaderboard loading at ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:142-158 and is collapsed into this finding.
attack_scenario: On every launch, an interceptor returns a very large number of valid 11-line records or one extremely long first line. readLine() and the lists grow until memory is exhausted; if the response eventually ends, the quadratic sort can consume prolonged CPU. The app may be killed for memory pressure or remain busy without ever making shared levels available.
preconditions: The app must see an active network and initiate the automatic level request; the platform must permit the HTTP connection; the attacker must control its response.
validation_plan: Proxy get_level.php and generate increasingly large but syntactically valid 11-line records with equal numeric values. Launch the app while recording heap use and the loader thread. Confirmation is unbounded heap growth, an OutOfMemoryError/process kill, or sustained execution in ApoClockUserlevels.java:57-74 after EOF. Separately, withhold EOF or newlines to confirm there is no read timeout.

title: Online leaderboard accepts scores asserted entirely by the client
entry_point: The player-controlled client supplies name, points, and clock count. Arcade computes points only in local mutable state at ApoClockArcardeGame.java:219-237, while the name is taken from the local text field at ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89.
sink: ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save() writes the three values directly to save_highscore.php at lines 81-100 with no session identifier, gameplay proof, nonce, signature, or authenticator in the request body at lines 92-96.
data_path: A completed Arcade game calls ApoClockPanel.setAracardeHelp() at ApoClockArcardeGame.java:250-267; ApoClockPanel.java:253-263 invokes ApoClockArcarde.setPoints(); ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89 calls ApoClockHighscore.saveHighscore(); its thread at ApoClockHighscore.java:64-75 reaches ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save().
attack_scenario: A cheating player intercepts their own score POST or instruments the app, replaces points with a much larger integer, and forwards the request. Because the request carries only client assertions, the server has no submitted evidence from which to reconstruct the run. If save_highscore.php stores such requests, the attacker obtains a forged shared leaderboard position.
preconditions: The endpoint must be reachable and persist client submissions. Server-side range or rate checks could limit particular values, but no server implementation was supplied; independent verification of the claimed run is impossible from the three submitted fields alone.
validation_plan: Against an authorized staging or cloned endpoint, complete any qualifying Arcade run through an HTTP proxy and change the points field before forwarding. Then request get_highscore.php and confirm the modified value appears. Repeat with a direct form POST to determine whether the endpoint requires any state not present in the client request.

title: Unlocked progression is trusted directly from local preferences
code_excerpt:
int solved = ApoClock.settings.getInt("solved", 0);
		this.solvedLevel(solved);
entry_point: The local ApoClockPref SharedPreferences file opened with mode 0 at ApoClock.java:39 supplies the solved integer when the app starts.
sink: ApoClockPanel passes the value to solvedLevel() at ApoClockPanel.java:119-126 and 349-351. ApoClockPuzzleChooser.setSolved() trusts it and marks levels available at ApoClockPuzzleChooser.java:65-76; touch handling permits every index up to that value at lines 81-86.
data_path: A local user edits the solved entry in the app-private preference XML; ApoClockPanel.loadPreferences() reads it at lines 118-126; solvedLevel() calls ApoClockPuzzleChooser.setSolved(); and the chooser uses the resulting field as its only progression gate.
attack_scenario: On a rooted or debuggable device, a player stops the app, changes the solved preference to 29, and restarts it. Level 30 becomes selectable without completing the preceding levels. The gain is confined to cheating progression on that installation and does not itself forge the online leaderboard.
preconditions: The user needs root, run-as/debug access, a permitted backup/restore path, or another means to modify the app-private SharedPreferences file. An ordinary sandboxed application cannot edit another app's mode-0 preferences.
validation_plan: On a rooted or authorized debuggable emulator, stop net.apogames.apoclock, edit shared_prefs/ApoClockPref.xml so solved is 29, restart, and open the puzzle chooser. Confirm that the last built-in level is selectable before any earlier level is completed.

title: Shared levels are downloaded and uploaded over cleartext HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoDice4k/get_level.php";
	public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoDice4k/save_level.php";
entry_point: The remote level response enters through ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:153-182. Locally created level data enters the upload path through ApoDiceEditor.touchedButton()/uploadString() at ApoDiceEditor.java:138-158 and 185-188.
sink: URLConnection transmits and receives without TLS in ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.save() at lines 121-137 and load() at lines 162-179.
data_path: Startup calls ApoDicePanel.init() -> loadUserlevels() (ApoDicePanel.java:58-60,79-86) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.loadUserlevels() (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:22-30) -> ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() (lines 153-209). Upload follows ApoDiceEditor.uploadString() (ApoDiceEditor.java:185-188) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.addLevel() (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:83-89) -> ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.save() (lines 113-143).
attack_scenario: On an attacker-controlled Wi-Fi network, the attacker intercepts the HTTP request to the endpoint defined at ApoDiceConstants.java:5. They replace the level feed with attacker-chosen, syntactically complete 11-line records. The client stores those strings at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-205 and exposes them as playable levels at ApoDiceUserlevels.java:27-32. The attacker can inject or censor shared content and can combine this with ApoDice-02 to crash the game. The same attacker can alter an outgoing level upload sent at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:130-133.
preconditions: The device must report an active connection through ApoDice.isOnline() (ApoDice.java:48-52), the Android build/platform must permit cleartext traffic, and the attacker must control the server or the network path.
validation_plan: In an authorized emulator, route www.apo-games.de through an intercepting proxy or test DNS mapping. Return a valid 11-line level record different from the legitimate response, launch the app, and tap userlevels. Seeing the injected level in the game and its plaintext request/response in the proxy proves the path. Repeat an editor upload and verify that the form body is readable and modifiable in transit.

title: Downloaded level shorter than 64 characters crashes level loading
entry_point: Every eleventh response line is accepted as a level string without length or alphabet validation at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-185.
sink: ApoDicePuzzleGame.loadLevel() indexes all positions 0 through 63 with String.charAt() at line 187.
data_path: ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the response string (lines 182-185) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() copies it into ApoDiceLevel.editorLevels (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:27-30,44-54) -> the userlevels button invokes ApoDicePanel.setPuzzleGame() (ApoDiceMenu.java:75-76; ApoDicePanel.java:136-146) -> loadLevel() selects editorLevels[p[1]] and calls charAt() (ApoDicePuzzleGame.java:176-187).
attack_scenario: A malicious server or network attacker returns one complete 11-line record whose first line is just "0" and whose numeric metadata lines are valid. Loading succeeds and the userlevels button appears. When the victim taps it, charAt(0) succeeds but charAt(1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoDicePuzzleGame.java:187; no variant code catches the exception on this path, disrupting or crashing the game.
preconditions: The attacker must cause the shared-level endpoint to return a short level string, either by controlling the service/content or by altering the cleartext response identified in ApoDice-01, and the victim must select userlevels.
validation_plan: Serve an authorized test response containing these eleven fields in order: level "0", time 1.0, count 1, total 1, any name, four integer ratings, ID 1, and current time 1.0. Launch the app, wait for userlevels to become visible, and tap it. A logcat StringIndexOutOfBoundsException pointing to ApoDicePuzzleGame.loadLevel() line 187 confirms the issue.

title: Unbounded level-feed response can exhaust application memory
entry_point: A malicious level server or network attacker controls the response stream returned by urlConn.getInputStream() at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:179.
sink: The EOF-controlled loop at lines 182-207 reads unbounded line lengths and appends an unbounded number of strings and boxed numeric values to eleven ArrayLists.
data_path: ApoDicePanel.init() automatically starts loadUserlevels() at ApoDicePanel.java:58-60; its thread calls ApoDiceUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at lines 79-86, which calls ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() at ApoDiceUserlevels.java:22-25. The response then enters the unbounded read-and-append loop at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:179-207.
attack_scenario: The attacker continuously sends valid 11-line records, or sends one extremely large first line, without closing the response. Because neither line length nor record count is capped at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207, heap usage grows until the Android process raises OutOfMemoryError and terminates. This load begins automatically rather than requiring a level-selection tap.
preconditions: The app must be online, cleartext traffic must be permitted, and the attacker must control the endpoint or HTTP response path long enough to stream the payload.
validation_plan: In a test emulator with a constrained heap, redirect the endpoint to a lab server that streams repeated valid 11-line records indefinitely. Launch the app and monitor `adb shell dumpsys meminfo` and logcat. Monotonically growing heap followed by OutOfMemoryError originating from readLine or the ArrayList additions confirms the weakness.

title: Editable SharedPreferences value unlocks every built-in level
code_excerpt:
int solved = settings.getInt("solved", 0);
		this.solvedLevel(solved);
entry_point: A local user with access to the app-private preferences file can modify the `solved` integer in ApoDicePref, whose name is defined at ApoDiceConstants.java:11 and opened at ApoDice.java:43.
sink: ApoDicePuzzleChooser.setSolved() trusts the stored value and clamps it only to MAX_LEVELS-1 at lines 66-74; touchedPressed() then permits every index less than or equal to that value at lines 83-87.
data_path: ApoDice.onCreate() opens the preferences (ApoDice.java:43) -> ApoDicePanel.init() calls loadPreferences() (ApoDicePanel.java:64) -> getInt() supplies the edited value (lines 67-69) -> solvedLevel() forwards it to ApoDicePuzzleChooser.setSolved() (ApoDicePanel.java:179-180; ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:66-77) -> the chooser authorizes level selection using i <= solved (ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:83-87).
attack_scenario: On a rooted emulator/device or an accessible debug installation, the user edits ApoDicePref.xml and sets `solved` to 2147483647. On relaunch, setSolved() clamps it to MAX_LEVELS-1 at ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:69-70, and the i <= solved check at lines 84-86 makes every built-in level selectable. The gain is progression cheating only.
preconditions: The attacker needs local access to app-private storage, such as root, emulator access, or a build permitting `run-as`/backup access. The supplied generated BuildConfig declares DEBUG=true at gen/net/apogames/apodice/BuildConfig.java:5, but the Android manifest is not present to independently verify debuggability.
validation_plan: Install the variant on a rooted test emulator, launch it once, force-stop it, and change the `solved` integer in shared_prefs/ApoDicePref.xml to 2147483647. Relaunch, open the puzzle chooser, and select the final built-in level without completing predecessors. Successful selection confirms the trust bypass.

title: Shared levels are uploaded and downloaded over unauthenticated HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/get_level.php";
public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/save_level.php";
entry_point: User-created levels originate in game/ApoMonoEditor.java:153-155. Downloaded, attacker-controlled response bytes enter through userlevels/ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:181-184.
sink: URLConnection sends and receives level data at userlevels/ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:122-138 and 164-184 using the HTTP URLs at ApoMonoConstants.java:7-8.
data_path: ApoMonoPanel.java:87-89 starts loadUserlevels(); ApoMonoPanel.java:367-374 creates the worker thread; ApoMonoUserlevels.java:22-30 calls ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() and publishes the returned strings as ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels. Uploads follow ApoMonoEditor.uploadString() at lines 153-157 through ApoMonoUserlevels.addLevel() at lines 85-91 to ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.save().
attack_scenario: An attacker controlling the server or an on-path Wi-Fi, proxy, DNS, or routing position intercepts the plaintext POST. They replace the get_level.php body with their own syntactically valid level record, which the client installs in editorLevels, or alter an uploaded level before it reaches save_level.php. This gives the attacker control over shared-level integrity and can feed the parser in finding ApoMonoAndroid-03.
preconditions: ApoMonoActivity.isOnline() must return true as implemented at ApoMonoActivity.java:69-73; the packaged application must have INTERNET permission and permit cleartext traffic; the attacker must control the endpoint or network path.
validation_plan: Run the app or a source-compatible harness through an intercepting HTTP proxy. If the historical host is unavailable, transparently route www.apo-games.de:80 to a local stub. Observe the plaintext Get= POST, return one valid 11-line record, and confirm ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels is populated and the user-level button becomes visible. Upload an editor level and confirm the proxy can read and change the level= form body without any TLS failure.

title: Unbounded level-server response can exhaust heap and CPU
entry_point: A malicious server or plaintext-network attacker controls the response stream returned by urlConn.getInputStream() at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:181.
sink: The EOF-terminated loop at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-209 appends every response line to unbounded ArrayLists. After EOF, ApoMonoUserlevels.java:61-75 performs insertion-style sorting with a nested loop over all accepted levels.
data_path: ApoMonoPanel.init() automatically calls loadUserlevels() at ApoMonoPanel.java:87-89; its worker at lines 367-374 calls ApoMonoUserlevels.loadUserlevels(), then ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load(), readLine(), the ArrayList add operations, and sortByUpload(). No user selection is required.
attack_scenario: The attacker serves hundreds of thousands of complete 11-line records or keeps sending records without EOF. The loader retains every line in eleven growing lists; if the body eventually ends, the quadratic sort adds sustained CPU use. The attacker gains a remotely triggered application hang or OutOfMemoryError/process termination.
preconditions: The same network and cleartext preconditions as ApoMonoAndroid-01 apply. The attacker must keep the HTTP connection open or supply a sufficiently large response.
validation_plan: Route get_level.php to a controlled HTTP stub. Repeatedly emit an 11-line record consisting of level 000, numeric values for the float/integer slots, and a short name, either indefinitely or for several hundred thousand records. Launch the online app and monitor adb shell dumpsys meminfo plus logcat. Monotonic heap growth, prolonged sorting after EOF, an OutOfMemoryError, or process death confirms the finding.

title: Downloaded level strings reach fixed-position parsing without format validation
entry_point: The first line of every network record is accepted as a level at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-186.
sink: ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel() performs unchecked substring conversion at lines 240-242 and unchecked l.charAt(cur) access at line 248.
data_path: ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the network line; ApoMonoUserlevels.sortByUpload() checks only s.length() > 2 at lines 61-64; getAllLevelsSorted() publishes it at lines 44-56. A tap on the user-level menu invokes ApoMonoMenu.java:59-60, ApoMonoPanel.setGame() at lines 249-262, and ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel(), where fixed-position parsing occurs.
attack_scenario: The attacker returns a complete 11-line server record whose level line is x00 and whose remaining numeric fields are valid. The record passes the length check and makes the user-level menu available. When the player selects it, Integer.valueOf("x") throws NumberFormatException on line 240. A three-digit numeric level such as 000 instead reaches charAt(3) at line 248 and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The attacker gains a repeatable client crash after one menu action.
preconditions: The attacker must control the level-server response through server compromise or the plaintext channel, provide all eleven metadata lines so sorting succeeds, and the player must tap the downloaded user-level entry.
validation_plan: Serve one record with lines: x00, 1, 1, 1, name, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1. Launch the app online, wait for the user-level button, tap it, and capture logcat. A NumberFormatException whose stack reaches ApoMonoPuzzleGame.java:240 proves the path. Repeat with level 000 to confirm StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 248.

title: Tampered solved-level preference directly controls progression gates
entry_point: The locally stored SharedPreferences value named solvedLevels is read at game/ApoMonoPanel.java:134-135. The preference store is created at ApoMonoActivity.java:37.
sink: ApoMonoLevelChooser.java:64 copies ApoMonoPanel.getMaxCanChoosen() into canStart, and lines 83-84 use canStart as the gate for starting a level.
data_path: ApoMonoPanel.loadPreferences() reads the string and calls ApoMonoSave.createArrayFromString(); ApoMonoSave.java:30-34 increments solvedCout for every token, including duplicates; ApoMonoPanel.java:395-400 computes the unlocked limit as solvedCout + 2; ApoMonoLevelChooser.java:83-84 trusts that value.
attack_scenario: A local user with access to app-private data edits ApoMonoPref.xml and replaces solvedLevels with many repeated valid entries such as 0,0,0,... . On restart, each duplicate increments solvedCout even though only array element zero is set. The resulting count is capped only at the game's maximum and unlocks later levels without solving them. The gain is cheating in the local progression system, not privilege outside the game.
preconditions: The user needs app-data access, such as a rooted device, debug/emulator build with run-as or Device Explorer access, or a writable/restorable application-data backup. Stock unrooted release-app sandboxing would normally prevent direct XML editing.
validation_plan: On a debug emulator, stop the app and use run-as or Android Studio Device Explorer to set the ApoMonoPref shared-preference string solvedLevels to at least one hundred comma-separated zeroes. Restart, open the normal level chooser, and verify that levels far beyond the legitimate progress point can be selected. Inspect solvedCout or getMaxCanChoosen() to confirm that duplicate tokens, rather than distinct solved levels, produced the unlock.

title: Shared levels use unauthenticated cleartext HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/get_level.php";
	public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php";
entry_point: Downloaded bytes enter through urlConn.getInputStream()/input.readLine() at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:179-182; a locally authored level enters save(String level) at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:113 and is encoded at line 132.
sink: The fixed http URLs at ApoSnakeConstants.java:5-6 are passed to URL/openConnection and cleartext request/response streams at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:121-137 and 162-179.
data_path: Download: ApoSnakePanel.init() automatically calls loadUserlevels() at ApoSnakePanel.java:58-60; its thread at lines 79-86 calls ApoSnakeUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:22-30, then ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() at lines 153-209. Upload: ApoSnakeEditor.uploadString() at ApoSnakeEditor.java:227-230 calls ApoSnakeUserlevels.addLevel() at ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:84-90, then save() at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:113-143.
attack_scenario: An attacker controlling the level server, DNS/route, or the victim's Wi-Fi answers the startup HTTP request with altered 11-line level records; the client accepts them as shared levels. The same attacker can read, change, or drop the level= POST during upload. This gives control over downloaded game content and enables the parser and availability attacks described below.
preconditions: The build must grant network access and the Android version/network-security policy must permit cleartext HTTP; ApoSnake.isOnline() must return true (ApoSnake.java:48-52). A network-position attacker or malicious endpoint is needed; upload interception additionally requires the user to upload a solved editor level.
validation_plan: Run the app/emulator with an HTTP-intercepting proxy or map www.apo-games.de to a controlled HTTP server. Launch while connected and observe the POST to get_level.php, then create, solve, and upload a level and observe the readable level= body sent to save_level.php. Modify the download response and confirm the altered level reaches the user-level menu; packet capture showing plaintext requests and successful response substitution proves the issue.

title: Malformed downloaded level strings crash the level decoder
entry_point: Every line with index 0 modulo 11 from the HTTP response is stored verbatim as a level at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:182-185.
sink: ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel() derives array dimensions without checking length or range at lines 159-161, then indexes every declared cell with l.charAt(...) at line 167 and again at line 195.
data_path: ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the response at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:179-205; ApoSnakeUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() copies it at ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:44-56 and assigns ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels at line 30. The userlevels button invokes setPuzzleGame(-1, "", true) at ApoSnakeMenu.java:75-76; ApoSnakePanel.setPuzzleGame() calls loadLevel() at ApoSnakePanel.java:136-146, which selects editorLevels[p[0]] at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:138-155 and reaches the unchecked decoder.
attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP man-in-the-middle returns one otherwise valid 11-line record whose level line is aa. Loading succeeds and exposes the userlevels button. When the victim taps it, width and height become 1, but l.charAt(2) at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:167 reads past the two-character string. The exception escapes every supplied caller and yields a repeatable game crash. A header byte such as _ produces a negative array dimension at line 161.
preconditions: The network path in ApoSnake-01 must operate, the attacker must supply valid numeric values for the other ten record lines so sorting completes, and the victim must open userlevels. Direct poisoning by an ordinary UGC author is not established because save_level.php is not in the supplied source.
validation_plan: Intercept get_level.php and serve these 11 lines in order: aa, 1.0, 1, 1, attacker, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1.0. Launch, wait for userlevels to appear, and tap it. An IndexOutOfBoundsException/StringIndexOutOfBoundsException with ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:167 in the stack, or process termination at that action, confirms reachability.

title: Unbounded shared-level response can exhaust memory and CPU
entry_point: The server-controlled HTTP body enters DataInputStream at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:179 and is consumed until EOF at lines 182-207.
sink: There is no response, line-length, or record-count bound before readLine() and the eleven ArrayList.add/valueOf branches at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:182-205; after reading, sortByUpload() performs nested insertion scanning at ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:61-75.
data_path: ApoSnakePanel.init() starts the download without a user gesture at ApoSnakePanel.java:58-60 and 79-86. ApoSnakeUserlevels.loadUserlevels() calls load() and then sortByUpload() at ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:22-30, so attacker-controlled response size directly controls retained strings, boxed numbers, and the quadratic sort workload.
attack_scenario: A malicious endpoint or HTTP man-in-the-middle streams a very long first line or hundreds of thousands of syntactically valid 11-line records. readLine() and the lists keep allocating until heap exhaustion; if EOF is sent first, equal timestamps make the nested insertion sort scan all prior entries and consume quadratic CPU. Because loading starts during initialization, the attacker can freeze or kill the game on launch without a menu selection.
preconditions: The network and cleartext preconditions from ApoSnake-01 must hold and the attacker must control or replace the get_level.php response. A sufficiently large body relative to the Android heap is required.

title: Eight-byte level header can drive multi-gigabyte image allocation
entry_point: An editable default level is loaded automatically from user.dir/levels/Original_First.defence (ApoDefenceGame.java:176), and arbitrary local .defence files can also be selected through the Load chooser (ApoDefenceOptions.java:170-172; ApoDefenceGame.java:347-362).
sink: Unvalidated dimensions control new int[y][x] in readLevel() (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:156-164) and subsequently new BufferedImage(x*32, y*32, TYPE_INT_RGB) (ApoDefenceGame.java:210-225).
data_path: The file chooser or automatic startup path reaches ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel(). It reads two signed integers without bounds or overflow checks and allocates the grid (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:145-164). If the file ends there, EOFException is logged but no failure is returned or state rolled back (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:198-208). preconditions: The attacker can modify the default level file or persuade the user to open a malicious/user-generated .defence file. The JVM heap is smaller than the attacker-selected allocation, as is normal for the example dimensions.
validation_plan: Create oom.defence using DataOutputStream.writeInt(1000) twice and no further bytes. Confirmation is an EOFException message followed by an uncaught OutOfMemoryError or allocation failure whose stack includes ApoDefenceGame.makeNewXAndY()/BufferedImage. The loader accepts it as a level-only partial record, sorting fails and silently nulls the singleton reference. preconditions: The online response must be attacker-controlled and contain 1-4 trailing lines modulo five; the player must click User Levels after the asynchronous load finishes.
validation_plan: Point the JVM at a local mock HTTP proxy, answer get_highscore.php with the single line "1\n", then EOF. Wait for the loader thread and click User Levels. A NullPointerException from ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.getLevel near line 112 followed by a stopped ApoSubGame thread confirms the full path.

title: Dormant URLClassLoader instantiates caller-selected code
entry_point: There is no stock-game entry point: the public constructor accepts path and classname at org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:19-21, but the whole-tree reference scan found no construction or getMyClass call outside this class.
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:69-75 executes the selected class initializer and constructor.
data_path: Theoretical only: constructor path and classname (:19-21) -> getMyClass -> local File URL when B_APPLET is false or arbitrary URL when true (:62-69) -> loadClass (:73) -> newInstance (:75). No untrusted network response, local file, chooser selection, or command-line argument reaches this method in the shipped variant.
attack_scenario: This cannot be triggered in the stock game. If an external caller or future clone wires a user-selected directory or URL and class name into this helper, the attacker places a class there; getMyClass loads it and its constructor executes with the game's JVM permissions, yielding arbitrary code execution.
preconditions: New integration code or an external harness must call ApoClassLoader. Remote URL loading additionally requires ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true; desktop mode loads from a local filesystem URL.
validation_plan: For a proof of the dormant sink, compile a test class whose constructor creates a marker file, place it under a temporary class-root directory, and invoke new ApoClassLoader(tempRoot, "test.Payload").getMyClass() from a harness. Marker creation proves execution. Then confirm the unmodified game never invokes the harness or helper.

title: Applet progress can be forged over plain HTTP
entry_point: A server-controlled or intercepted response from http://www.apo-games.de/apoRelax/cookies.php during applet startup. ApoRelaxApplet.java:27-29 enables applet mode and ApoRelaxApplet.java:39-48 invokes panel initialization.
sink: ApoRelaxLevelChooser.setMaxLevel(int) at ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:119-124 accepts the returned integer as the unlocked-level boundary.
data_path: ApoRelaxApplet.init at ApoRelaxApplet.java:39-48 calls ApoRelaxPanel.init; ApoRelaxPanel.java:90-95 calls ApoHelp.loadData; ApoHelp.java:446-465 opens the HTTP connection and returns its first line; ApoRelaxPanel.java:94-95 parses it and passes it to setMaxLevel. ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:203-205 then renders levels through that boundary.
attack_scenario: An on-path attacker intercepts the cleartext cookies.php request and returns the single line "11". The client parses it and displays all twelve built-in levels as unlocked, modifying the victim's progression without solving them. The same cleartext channel is used to save progress at ApoRelaxPanel.java:208-218.
preconditions: The bundled JApplet entry point must be used so ApoConstants.B_APPLET is true, and the attacker must control apo-games.de or the victim's HTTP path. The normal desktop entry point leaves this branch disabled.
validation_plan: Run the applet through a legacy JRE with an intercepting proxy. Return HTTP 200 and body "11\n" for /apoRelax/cookies.php. Open the level chooser and confirm that levels 1-12 are drawn as unlocked. Capturing the request also confirms that no TLS protects the response.

title: Unbounded HTTP line read can exhaust or hang the applet
code_excerpt:
BufferedReader iStream = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(con.getInputStream()));
retVal = iStream.readLine();
entry_point: The response stream from the applet's progress endpoint, controlled by a malicious apo-games.de server or an HTTP on-path attacker.
sink: BufferedReader.readLine() at ApoHelp.java:465 reads without a length bound, connect timeout, or read timeout.
data_path: ApoRelaxApplet.java:48 calls ApoRelaxPanel.init; ApoRelaxPanel.java:93 invokes ApoHelp.loadData; ApoHelp.java:452-465 opens the connection and synchronously reads one unrestricted line before game startup continues. The same root cause appears in saveData at ApoHelp.java:424-436.
attack_scenario: The attacker returns an endless response body without a newline, or opens the response and stops sending data. Applet initialization remains blocked; if bytes continue arriving, readLine grows its buffer until the game process exhausts heap memory.
preconditions: Applet mode must be used and the progress request must reach a malicious server or traverse an attacker-controlled plain-HTTP connection.
validation_plan: Route www.apo-games.de through a test proxy/server that responds to /apoRelax/cookies.php with an endless chunked stream of 'A' bytes and no newline. Start the applet with a small heap such as -Xmx64m. A startup hang followed by increasing heap use or OutOfMemoryError confirms the issue.

title: Editor decodes full-size images before enforcing its size cap
code_excerpt: img = ImageIO.read(new File(pic));
entry_point: A local image selected through the desktop editor's file chooser at ApoRelaxEditor.java:221-226, including an image downloaded from an untrusted source.
sink: ImageIO.read(File) decodes and allocates the complete attacker-specified raster before any dimension limit is applied.
data_path: ApoRelaxEditor.loadImage at ApoRelaxEditor.java:221-226 gets the chosen path and calls ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage; ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.java:513-515 delegates through ApoRelaxImages.getImage and ApoImageFromValue.getImageFromPath to ApoImage.getPic; ApoImage.java:88-94 performs ImageIO.read. title: Locked levels remain clickable while hidden
entry_point: Mouse press/release coordinates supplied by the local player while the level chooser is open.
sink: ApoRelaxPanel.setGame(i) is invoked at ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:147 without checking i against maxLevel.

title: Dormant URLClassLoader executes unauthenticated classes
entry_point: There is no production entry point in ApoRelax. The public constructor parameters path and classname at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21 would be the input source, but a whole-tree reference search found no instantiation of ApoClassLoader.
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75 loads and executes the selected class without signature or hash verification.
data_path: A hypothetical caller supplies path and classname to ApoClassLoader.java:19-21 and invokes getMyClass. In applet mode, ApoClassLoader.java:65-69 treats path as a URL; lines 73-75 load and instantiate the class. No current menu, network response, command-line argument, or file parser calls this API.
attack_scenario: Theoretical only: if this cloned helper is later wired to downloaded level or plugin metadata, an attacker hosts a class directory or JAR, supplies its URL and class name, and gains code execution through the class initializer or constructor. The present ApoRelax game offers no way to supply those values or invoke getMyClass.
preconditions: A new or external caller must invoke the helper with attacker-controlled values; ApoConstants.B_APPLET must be true for an HTTP URL; and the runtime must permit URLClassLoader access. These conditions are not met by this variant.
validation_plan: To prove the dormant primitive, build a test class whose static initializer writes a marker file, serve its package directory from a local HTTP server, set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true in a harness, and call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/", "test.Payload").getMyClass(). The marker proves execution; separately confirm that no ApoRelax source instantiates ApoClassLoader.

title: Highscores, shared levels, player names, and telemetry use plain HTTP
code_excerpt: public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSheeptastic/get_highscore.php";
entry_point: Player-controlled name, level, and score values originate in ApoSimpleGame.uploadScore (ApoSimpleGame.java:962-973), while server-controlled highscore and level bytes enter through ApoHighscore.load (ApoHighscore.java:148-164) and ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load (ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:137-153).

ApoSimplePanel initialization starts highscore and user-level retrieval at ApoSimplePanel.java:202,205-206 and sends start telemetry containing getTextName() at ApoSimplePanel.java:227. The endpoint constants for highscore, one-button highscore, and shared levels are all HTTP at ApoConstants.java:21-28.

The modified level data is accepted at ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-150 and can reach the parser and solver described in ApoSimple-02 and ApoSimple-03.

validation_plan: Launch the game with a transparent or JVM HTTP proxy, allow initialization, and capture requests to get_highscore.php, get_level.php, and game_counter.php. Confirm that name/score/form data is readable without TLS, then return an altered five-line level record and verify that ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad stores it at lines 140-150.

title: Invalid shared-level cells trigger combinatorial solver CPU exhaustion
entry_point: A length-valid level string supplied by get_level.php and stored at ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-142.
sink: The recursive search at ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:33-94, combined with the per-candidate movement loop at lines 143-239.
data_path: ApoSimpleLevel accepts every numeric two-character cell value without checking its domain at ApoSimpleLevel.java:86-97. After the selected level reaches ApoSimplePanel.setLevel at ApoSimplePanel.java:687-695, ApoSimpleLevelGame starts getMinSolution with maxSteps 4 in a new thread at ApoSimpleLevelGame.java:113-119. Unknown values qualify as candidate cells at ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:38-49 and fall through getDirection unchanged at line 274, so each candidate can consume the 200-step guard at lines 232-238 while the recursive branch at lines 71-90 explores further candidates.
attack_scenario: The attacker returns a level field made from "99" repeated 49 times plus "999" for the stars, followed by valid metadata. All 49 cells are numeric but outside the defined 0-25 domain (ApoSimpleConstants.java:366-396). Selecting the level starts a 49-way, four-move search in which invalid cells do not move or become solved, causing millions of candidate simulations and sustained CPU consumption.
preconditions: The attacker controls the shared-level HTTP response or gets this record accepted by the shared server, and the player selects the malicious level. Runtime duration depends on hardware, but no early solution exists for the all-99 grid because invalid cells remain nonempty under ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:245-249.
validation_plan: Serve a five-line record whose first line is `"99" * 49 + "999"` and whose remaining lines are `0`, `1`, `1`, and `0`. Select Userlevels and record process CPU plus thread stacks. Confirmation is a solver thread remaining in ApoSimpleLevelSolution.canBeSolved/getMinSolution, repeatedly reaching the line-237 step guard; terminate the test rather than waiting for completion.

title: Any completed highscore response is treated as success and grants coins
entry_point: An HTTP response controlled by save_highscore.php, a network attacker, or a local cheater's proxy (ApoHighscore.java:99-105).
sink: The coin balance increase in ApoSimpleGame.uploadScore at ApoSimpleGame.java:975-977.
data_path: The upload button starts uploadScore at ApoSimpleGame.java:895-903. uploadScore invokes ApoHighscore.save at line 973. ApoHighscore discards every response line and returns true solely because the stream reached EOF at ApoHighscore.java:99-105; the caller then adds ADD_COINS_UPLOAD, defined as 50 at ApoSimpleConstants.java:16.
attack_scenario: A local cheater routes the hard-coded HTTP endpoint through a controlled proxy, clicks Upload after reaching the score screen, and answers the POST with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and an empty completed body. The response loop executes zero times, save returns true, and the client grants 50 spendable hint coins even though no score was stored.
preconditions: The player reaches the score-upload UI, and the attacker can answer the HTTP request. No specific response text is required; the response must merely let getInputStream complete without IOException.
validation_plan: Intercept save_highscore.php with a local HTTP proxy, return status 200 with Content-Length 0, click Upload, and compare the displayed balance before and after. A 50-coin increase at ApoSimpleGame.java:977 confirms the finding.

title: Editable properties file directly sets spendable coin balance

entry_point: The user-editable `properties` file in the desktop process's working directory, loaded at ApoSimplePanel.java:216-220.

Three booleans are read first and the following unverified int is assigned as coins at ApoSimpleProperties.java:47-50. If the file ends there, ApoIO silently catches EOF at lines 88-89 after the balance has already changed.

validation_plan: Close the game, preserve the original file, place the seven specified bytes in `properties` in the launch directory, and restart through ApoSimpleMain. Confirm that renderCoins displays 1000000 at ApoSimplePanel.java:897-907 and that a hint purchase succeeds through ApoSimpleGame.java:246-264.

title: Local levels file supplies an unchecked negative button index
entry_point: The user-editable `levels` binary file opened when the desktop player enters the level chooser (ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:50-56).
sink: buttons.get(level-1) in ApoSimpleLevelChooser.setVisibleButtons at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:136-140.

After buttons are created, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.init calls setVisibleButtons at line 126, where the parsed level becomes a list index.

Parsing succeeds, but entering the level chooser evaluates buttons.get(-1), throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException on the uncaught game loop. In-range fabricated records can likewise mark levels visible at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:137-140.

title: Dormant URLClassLoader can instantiate remote code but has no shipped call site
code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } );
entry_point: The public constructor's path and classname parameters at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21. Repository-wide reference search found no construction or method call outside this class, so there is no shipped untrusted entry point.
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75.
data_path: The constructor stores caller-controlled path and classname at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21, getMyClass converts path to a local file URL in desktop mode or a direct URL in applet mode at lines 62-69, then loads and instantiates the named class at lines 73-75. ApoSimpleMain.java:17-32 and ApoSimpleApplet.java:39-48 do not invoke this helper.
attack_scenario: This is theoretical in ApoSimple as shipped: no game UI, save parser, or network response reaches the constructor. If future integration passes an attacker URL and class name, the attacker hosts a class whose static initializer or constructor executes when getMyClass reaches lines 73-75, gaining code execution within the game's JVM permissions.
preconditions: A new caller, external harness, or future clone modification must invoke ApoClassLoader with attacker-controlled parameters; that prerequisite is absent from this variant.

title: Applet progress is loaded and saved over plain HTTP

sink: ApoHelp.loadData/saveData opens an HttpURLConnection at ApoHelp.java:424-425 and 452-455. The supplied base URL is the literal "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSudoku/" at ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.java:28.

title: Unbounded HTTP response line can hang or exhaust the game process
code_excerpt:
BufferedReader iStream = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(con.getInputStream()));
			retVal = iStream.readLine();
entry_point: A malicious apo-games.de server or HTTP interceptor controls the cookies.php response consumed by ApoHelp.loadData at ApoHelp.java:464-465 and saveData at lines 435-436.
sink: BufferedReader.readLine at ApoHelp.java:465 and 436 reads without a response-size bound. The URL connections created at lines 425 and 454 have no connect or read timeout configured.
data_path: Applet Play -> ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.init creates the loading thread (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:65-72) -> loadCookies (lines 133-149) -> ApoHelp.loadData -> readLine (ApoHelp.java:464-465). A second synchronous route is puzzle completion -> checkWin (ApoSimpleSudokuGame.java:176-179) -> saveCookies (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:159-178) -> ApoHelp.saveData -> readLine (ApoHelp.java:435-436).
attack_scenario: For the load route, the attacker streams a very large response without a newline; readLine keeps accumulating data and can consume the shared JVM heap. Alternatively, the attacker sends millions of comma-terminated integers: the unbounded loop at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:144-149 stores every value in solvedLevels. For the save route, accepting the connection but never completing the response blocks the game-loop thread after a level is solved.

On the Play request, continuously send "128," without a newline and monitor heap growth until an OutOfMemoryError or process failure occurs. Separately, return an empty initial progress line, solve level 1, accept the save request without sending a response, and confirm through a thread dump and frozen rendering that the game loop is blocked in BufferedReader.readLine.

title: Dormant URL class loader instantiates arbitrary external classes
entry_point: There is no untrusted in-game entry point. The only input surface is the public ApoClassLoader(path, classname) constructor at ApoClassLoader.java:19-22, which currently has no call site elsewhere in the 43-file variant.
sink: getMyClass converts the supplied path into a local or remote URL at ApoClassLoader.java:64-69, loads the supplied class name at line 73, and executes its initialization/constructor through newInstance at line 75.
data_path: Theoretical only: an embedding or future caller supplies path and classname -> constructor stores them (ApoClassLoader.java:19-22,36-37,52-53) -> getMyClass selects File.toURL or new URL (lines 62-69) -> URLClassLoader.loadClass (line 73) -> Class.newInstance (line 75). ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:29-40 defines a .class chooser, but its getters at lines 62-94 are never called and there is no showOpenDialog/getSelectedFile-to-loader path.
attack_scenario: Not exploitable through the shipped game. If reused code later passes an attacker-selected directory or HTTP base URL and class name, the attacker places a class there whose static initializer or public constructor runs commands; getMyClass then executes it with the game's JVM privileges.
preconditions: A new caller must be added or an embedding application must invoke ApoClassLoader with attacker-controlled path and classname. Merely placing a .class file beside the current game is insufficient because this variant never calls the loader.
validation_plan: Create evil.Payload with a public no-argument constructor that writes a marker file, compile it under a served directory, and use a small harness to set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true and invoke new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/", "evil.Payload").getMyClass(). The marker confirms code execution. Then verify that normal desktop and applet UI operation never requests Payload, confirming the finding remains theoretical in this variant.

title: Shared-level downloads and uploads use cleartext HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/save_highscore.php";
entry_point: Startup automatically requests shared levels through ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels at apoSlitherLink/game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:125-141. A solved editor puzzle is submitted when the Upload button reaches ApoSlitherLinkEditor.mouseButtonFunction at apoSlitherLink/game/ApoSlitherLinkEditor.java:112-121.

The gain is disclosure or manipulation of shared puzzle content, not host code execution.
preconditions: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE remains true as initialized at org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:23, and the endpoint is reachable directly or through an attacker-controlled network path.
validation_plan: Run the game with an intercepting HTTP proxy configured through the JVM http.proxyHost/http.proxyPort properties. Trigger startup and an editor upload. Confirm that the proxy can read and modify the POST parameters and can replace the GET response with a valid three-line record that subsequently appears under Custom.

title: Unbounded HTTP response is retained until heap exhaustion
entry_point: Response bytes from the cleartext get_highscore.php request opened at org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:109-126.
sink: The loop at ApoHighscore.java:129-138 has no response-size, line-length, or record-count limit and retains every line in one of three ArrayLists.
data_path: ApoSlitherLinkPanel.init creates the level I/O object and invokes loadLevels at ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:111-114; loadLevels starts a thread and calls ApoHighscore.load at lines 133-141; load reads and stores lines at ApoHighscore.java:126-138.
attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP interceptor returns an endless sequence of newline-delimited values, or one extremely large unterminated line. The startup thread continually allocates strings and grows the singleton's lists until an OutOfMemoryError or severe garbage-collection thrashing makes the game unusable.
preconditions: Online mode is enabled at ApoConstants.java:23 and the attacker can control or intercept the HTTP response. No player interaction is required after launch.
validation_plan: Proxy get_highscore.php to a local HTTP responder that continuously emits distinct short lines without closing the response. Launch with a small heap such as -Xmx64m. Confirm monotonically increasing heap use followed by OutOfMemoryError in the load thread or an unresponsive game.

ignored
attacker
". Wait for the startup request to complete, click Custom, and confirm NegativeArraySizeException points to ApoSlitherLinkLevel.java:425 and the game stops updating.

title: Editable save file can mark built-in puzzles solved without verification
entry_point: The user-editable relative file highscore.apo, fixed at apoSlitherLink/game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:26 and opened during desktop startup at ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:125-128.
sink: ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.checkLevelsIsIn unconditionally invokes setBSolved(true) at line 32 after matching only the public level string; it never proves that the supplied solution solves the puzzle.

attack_scenario: A local user writes one record containing the built-in level string from ApoSlitherLinkLevels.java:24 and the syntactically valid but empty-edge solution "0404aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"; "a" denotes an empty cell at ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:13. On restart, the game marks that Easy puzzle solved and increments the displayed completion count without the user solving it.
preconditions: Desktop mode is used and the attacker or cheating user can place highscore.apo in the process working directory before launch.
validation_plan: Use DataOutputStream to create highscore.apo with writeInt(1), writeUTF("0404  32 3     2 0 0"), and writeUTF("0404aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"). Launch from that directory and confirm the Easy completion counter is incremented and the first level is shown as solved despite the empty loop.

title: Unbounded save count amplifies into retained preview images
entry_point: The attacker-controlled highscore.apo file opened during desktop startup at ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:125-128 and org/apogames/ApoIO.java:215-229.
sink: The unchecked count controls the loop at ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.java:72-80. data_path: highscore.apo -> ApoIO.readLevel at ApoIO.java:210-229 -> ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.readLevel at lines 70-80 -> ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels at lines 125-132 -> ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.addCustomsLevels at lines 42-49 -> ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.makeSolvedImage at lines 166-264.

Duplicates are not filtered in addCustomsLevels at lines 43-49, and each retained helper receives a 200-by-200 ARGB preview at ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:10-11 and 254-264. validation_plan: Generate highscore.apo with writeInt(1000), followed by 1000 pairs of writeUTF("0101 ") and writeUTF("0101a"). Run with -Xmx64m. Confirm OutOfMemoryError during ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.makeSolvedImage or failure to reach the main menu.

title: Dormant URL class instantiation helper is theoretical
entry_point: There is no application entry point in this variant. The path and class name are accepted by the public constructor at org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:19-22, but no source file constructs ApoClassLoader or calls getMyClass.
sink: getMyClass creates a URLClassLoader, loads the selected class, and invokes its constructor at ApoClassLoader.java:62-75.
data_path: Theoretical only: a caller would pass path/classname to ApoClassLoader at lines 19-22, getMyClass would convert the path to a file URL or remote URL at lines 62-69, and loadClass/newInstance would execute the selected class at lines 73-75. The shipped ApoSlitherLink main path at ApoSlitherLinkMain.java:27-28 does not do this.
attack_scenario: No attacker-controlled input reaches this helper in the current variant, so there is no reproducible attack through the game UI, network loader, save file, or command line. If future wiring passes an attacker URL while B_APPLET is true, the attacker can serve a class whose constructor executes with the process's Java permissions.
preconditions: A new caller or test harness must invoke the otherwise-unused helper and allow an attacker to control both path and classname.
validation_plan: For a direct component test, compile evil.Payload with a constructor that creates a marker file, serve its package directory over local HTTP, set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true, and call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/", "evil.Payload").getMyClass(). The marker proves the sink works; a repository call-site search should still confirm it is not reachable from the shipped game.

title: properties.txt can auto-execute an arbitrary AI class
code_excerpt: c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);
entry_point: A local properties.txt supplies HomeAI or VisitorAI (ApoSoccerProperties.java:29-36); alternatively, the desktop "load AI" chooser supplies a selected .class path (ApoSoccerGame.java:1212-1218).
sink: ApoSoccerClassLoader.loadClass calls defineClass on the selected file bytes (ApoSoccerClassLoader.java:90-92), and getAI immediately calls Class.newInstance (ApoSoccerClassLoader.java:39-43).
data_path: ApoSoccerGame.init calls loadProperties (ApoSoccerGame.java:593); loadProperties reads properties.txt and calls loadPlayer with the stored path (ApoSoccerGame.java:620-630); loadPlayer derives the class name and directory (ApoSoccerGame.java:1224-1232), constructs ApoSoccerClassLoader (ApoSoccerGame.java:1257-1259), then getAI loads, defines, and instantiates the bytes.
attack_scenario: An attacker distributes a game/mod folder containing properties.txt with "HomeAI: Payload.class" and a malicious Payload.class. When the victim launches the desktop game from that folder, the class is instantiated during initialization; its static initializer or constructor executes with the game process's user permissions. A direct social-engineering variant asks the victim to choose the same file through "load Home AI".
preconditions: Desktop mode; the malicious class and configuration are in the launch working directory, or the user explicitly chooses the class; bytecode is compatible with the victim JVM. Extending ApoSoccerAI avoids the later cast failure, although constructor code runs before that cast.
validation_plan: Compile a Payload class extending ApoSoccerAI whose static initializer creates a harmless marker file. Put Payload.class and a properties.txt containing "HomeAI: Payload.class" in the launch directory, start ApoSoccerMain, and confirm the marker appears before any user interaction. Repeat through the load-AI chooser to confirm the second entry path.

title: Desktop startup loads an unverified DLL from user.dir
code_excerpt: System.load(lib);
entry_point: A local file named AIMultiplexer.dll in the process working directory, whose path comes from user.dir (ApoSoccerGame.java:583-586 and ApoSoccerConstants.java:324).
sink: ApoSoccerAIJNI.loadMultiplexer passes that path directly to System.load (ApoSoccerAIJNI.java:7-9).
data_path: ApoSoccerGame.init enters its desktop branch, concatenates System.getProperty("user.dir"), File.separator, and AIMultiplexer.dll, and calls loadMultiplexer (ApoSoccerGame.java:583-586); loadMultiplexer invokes System.load. The same feature also forwards chooser/properties-selected .dll or .so paths to the native loadAI method (ApoSoccerGame.java:1269-1274; ApoSoccerAIJNI.java:18-23).
attack_scenario: An attacker places or replaces AIMultiplexer.dll in a writable game launch directory, for example in a repackaged game archive. The victim starts ApoSoccer; Windows loads the attacker's DLL before the menu appears, executing its native initialization code with the victim's permissions.
preconditions: Desktop Windows deployment; the victim launches from a directory the attacker could populate or replace; the DLL matches the process architecture. For the secondary AI-DLL route, a legitimate multiplexer must first load.
validation_plan: Build a same-architecture test DLL whose DllMain or JNI_OnLoad writes a harmless marker, name it AIMultiplexer.dll, place it in a disposable launch directory, and start ApoSoccerMain from that directory. The marker appearing during ApoSoccerGame.init proves the startup path. Separately select a marker AI DLL to test the native loadAI route.

title: Replay track counts can crash playback or exhaust memory
entry_point: A user-selected, attacker-crafted .rep file reaches ApoSoccerReplay.loadReplay through the visible "replay load" button (ApoSoccerGame.java:363-369 and 889-892; ApoSoccerReplay.java:234-239).
sink: Playback bounds curStep only against the ball list (ApoSoccerReplay.java:308-310) and then indexes every independently sized player list with point.get(curStep) (ApoSoccerReplay.java:313-323 and 339-341).
data_path: The chooser path is passed to ApoSoccerReplayIO.readLevel (ApoSoccerReplay.java:235-238); readLevel reads nine independently attacker-sized tracks (ApoSoccerReplayIO.java:48-62); readPlayer accepts each signed count without a range or cross-track equality check (ApoSoccerReplayIO.java:112-120); replay play enters playStep via ApoSoccerGame.thinkGame (ApoSoccerGame.java:1760-1765).
attack_scenario: An attacker shares a syntactically complete replay with one ball point but zero points in each player track. The victim loads it and presses replay play. The ball-size guard passes at step zero, the first empty player list is indexed, and an uncaught IndexOutOfBoundsException terminates the game loop. A large positive count with enough coordinate bytes also creates unbounded ApoFloatPoint objects and can exhaust the heap.
preconditions: Desktop mode; the victim chooses the malicious .rep and starts playback. The small crash case needs only valid modified-UTF team names, ball count 1 with one x/y pair, and count 0 for each of the eight player tracks.
validation_plan: Create a binary replay using DataOutputStream: writeUTF("H"), writeUTF("V"), writeInt(1), two floats for the ball, then writeInt(0) eight times. Load it with "replay load", press "replay play", and confirm an IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSoccerReplay.setEntityPosition line 340 and cessation of the ApoThread loop. For memory impact, repeat under -Xmx128m with a large count and matching float pairs.

title: Applet team artwork is fetched over plaintext HTTP
entry_point: Image bytes returned by the fixed http://apo-games.de/apoSoccer/player/ team-asset locations used in applet mode (ApoSoccerGame.java:271-288 and 1051-1147).
sink: ApoImage.getImage gives the unauthenticated URL response directly to ImageIO.read with no TLS, integrity check, size limit, or connection/read timeout (ApoImage.java:78-113).
data_path: ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.init sets B_APPLET (ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.java:28-33); ApoSoccerGame assigns an http:// base when setting each AI (ApoSoccerGame.java:271-288); ApoTeam prefixes AI-provided emblem/player filenames with that base (ApoTeam.java:354-379); setAi or makeBackgroundWithEmblem requests the image (ApoTeam.java:279-284; ApoSoccerGame.java:738-753); ApoImage opens the URL.
attack_scenario: A network attacker intercepts the plaintext asset request and returns a different valid image, changing team/player artwork shown by the client. The attacker can instead delay the response or return an image with extreme decoded dimensions to stall or exhaust the game. This path does not expose a score-submission or credential channel in this variant.
preconditions: A legacy Java applet deployment is actually used, the selected AI returns a non-null emblem or custom player-image filename, and the attacker can intercept traffic to apo-games.de. The built-in AI implementations are not present in this source root, so their exact returned filenames could not be verified here.
validation_plan: Run the applet path or a harness with B_APPLET=true and an ApoSoccerAI whose getEmblem returns "emblem.png" under the game's fixed HTTP base. Intercept apo-games.de with a controlled proxy or DNS mapping, return a visibly different PNG, and confirm both the plaintext request and substituted emblem. A delayed response can confirm the synchronous no-timeout stall.

title: Dormant applet loader defines classes from arbitrary URL bytes
code_excerpt:
byte b[] = loadClassData(name);
			c = defineClass(b, 0, b.length);
entry_point: There is no source-visible untrusted entry point in the shipped applet flow. The primitive would receive a caller-supplied path and class name through the public ApoSoccerGame.loadPlayer overload (ApoSoccerGame.java:1253-1264).
sink: ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL downloads name + ".class" through URLConnection (ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL.java:75-102), calls defineClass (line 64), then Class.newInstance (lines 21-29).

Shipped applet buttons switch among already-linked AI objects through loadAI instead (ApoSoccerGame.java:923-946 and 1047-1149), while chooser and properties loading are disabled in applet mode (ApoSoccerGame.java:166-171 and 620-624).
attack_scenario: Theoretical only: if an embedding layer or future caller exposes the public loadPlayer parameters to untrusted input, an attacker supplies an HTTP base URL and a class name, serves a malicious compatible .class, and obtains code execution within the applet's Java protection domain. No such caller is present in the reviewed source.
preconditions: A non-shipped caller must invoke the public method with attacker-controlled values while B_APPLET is true; the runtime must permit the network connection and class definition; useful impact remains subject to the legacy applet sandbox/protection domain.
validation_plan: For the primitive, serve a Payload.class extending ApoSoccerAI from a local HTTP server, set B_APPLET=true in a test harness, call loadPlayer with that base URL and class name, and observe a harmless static-initializer marker. Separately retain the call-site search showing that normal applet UI paths call loadAI, not loadPlayer, to confirm current non-reachability.

title: Applet highscore and level traffic uses unauthenticated HTTP

URL connection				= new URL( fileName );
data						= new DataInputStream( connection.openStream() );
entry_point: ApoStarzApplet.init() at apoStarz/ApoStarzApplet.java:24-33. Its super.init() sets ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true at org/apogames/ApoApplet.java:34-39.
sink: URL.openStream() at org/apogames/ApoIO.java:220-221 for the binary highscore, URL.openStream() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzIO.java:102-103 for text levels, and HttpURLConnection.getOutputStream() at org/apogames/ApoIO.java:166-169 for highscore uploads.

Game.init() appends highscore.hig and calls ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel() at lines 144-147, which reaches ApoIO.readLevel() and openStream(). setNormalMode() at lines 432-435 and ApoStarzTutorial.init() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzTutorial.java:43-46 pass HTTP .ase URLs through ApoStarzGame.levelLoad(), ApoStarzIO.readLevel(), and its openStream(). The win path at ApoStarzGame.java:591-597 sends the binary highscore back through ApoIO.writeLevel().

A network attacker intercepts the plain-HTTP request for highscore.hig or an .ase file and returns a syntactically valid replacement containing attacker-selected scores, solutions, or level strings. The game consumes it without transport authentication, allowing leaderboard/content manipulation or a parser denial of service. The attacker can likewise observe or alter the cleartext highscore request body sent after a win.

validation_plan: Run ApoStarzApplet through an intercepting HTTP proxy or map apo-games.de to a controlled HTTP server. Serve a valid highscore.hig with a visibly altered score and a valid .ase file with a visibly altered level. Confirm requests are HTTP, not HTTPS, and confirm the altered values appear in the game. Complete a level and capture the cleartext request generated by ApoStarzGame.java:597 and ApoIO.java:166-174.

title: Four-character .ase level triggers a non-terminating parser loop
entry_point: A user-selected .ase file reaches ApoStarzGame.levelLoad() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:533-548 or ApoStarzEditor.levelLoad() at apoStarz/editor/ApoStarzEditor.java:306-314. In applet mode, HTTP-delivered level files reach the same path from ApoStarzGame.java:432-435 and ApoStarzTutorial.java:43-46.
sink: The coordinate-normalization loop at ApoStarzLevelLoad.java:209-211, whose decrement becomes zero when the parsed level width is 2.
data_path: ApoStarzIO.readLevel() reads each attacker-controlled line into allLevels at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzIO.java:95-108. ApoStarzGame.setLevelString() passes it to ApoStarzLevel.loadLevel() at ApoStarzGame.java:501-503 and ApoStarzLevel.java:243-245. ApoStarzLevelLoad.loadLevel() selects method one from the first character at lines 24-34; setWidth() converts the second character with width = c - 96 at lines 151-159; setWall() then enters the loop at lines 190-214.
attack_scenario: Create an .ase file whose first line is exactly ab"!. The first a selects method one, b produces width 2, the double quote declares one wall, and ! decodes to position 1. At line 209 the condition becomes 1 > 0, while line 211 repeatedly subtracts 0. Opening the file freezes the game thread and consumes a CPU core. A malicious level/highscore server can deliver the same level string to the applet.
preconditions: The victim must open the crafted .ase file, use a user-editable fixed level file, or run applet mode against a malicious/intercepted level or highscore response.
validation_plan: Put the single line ab"! in a file named hang.ase, launch the desktop game, choose Load, and select it. Run the process under a timeout and capture a thread dump. Continuous CPU use and a stack fixed at ApoStarzLevelLoad.setWall(), lines 209-211, confirm the issue.

title: Zero-record highscore file crashes game initialization
entry_point: The automatically loaded user.dir/levels/highscore.hig at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:144-150, or the applet's HTTP highscore response at line 147.
sink: ArrayList.get(0) on an empty levels list at ApoStarzHighscore.java:104.
data_path: ApoStarzGame.init() calls ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel(); org/apogames/ApoIO.java:209-224 opens the local file or URL and dispatches to ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel(). A four-byte zero count is accepted at ApoStarzHighscore.java:139-146 and leaves levels empty. Game.init() then calls setMenuMode() at ApoStarzGame.java:403, which calls getRandomLevel() at line 448 and reaches the unchecked get() sink.

On the next launch, the parser accepts a record count of zero. Menu initialization immediately requests a random level and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, preventing normal startup.

Confirm initialization terminates with IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoStarzHighscore.getRandomLevel() line 104. Repeat in applet mode by serving the same four-byte response.

title: Writable local highscore records have no integrity check
entry_point: The fixed user-editable file user.dir/levels/highscore.hig loaded by ApoStarzGame.init() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:144-150.
sink: The unverified score and solution are installed as authoritative ApoStarzHighscoreLevel values at ApoStarzHighscore.java:143-146. They are retrieved at lines 120-135 and displayed by ApoStarzGame.renderSteps() at ApoStarzGame.java:1060-1063.

On launch, the game accepts and displays the fabricated record as its highscore. This affects only the local game; the source does not establish that the desktop value reaches a shared server.

title: Dormant URL class loader can instantiate unsigned classes
entry_point: No shipped entry point. A repository-wide reference search found no construction or invocation outside ApoClassLoader.java itself.
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass() followed by Class.newInstance() at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75, which can initialize and construct code obtained from the configured URL.
data_path: A hypothetical caller supplies path and classname to the public constructor at ApoClassLoader.java:19-22 or setters at lines 36-38 and 52-54, sets applet mode so path is interpreted as a URL at lines 65-68, and calls getMyClass() at line 62.

If future integration passes an attacker-controlled URL and class name to this utility and invokes getMyClass(), the attacker can host a class whose static initializer or constructor executes with the game's process privileges.

validation_plan: First confirm the absence of callers with a full-source search for new ApoClassLoader and getMyClass. To demonstrate only the dormant capability, create a separate harness that sets ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true, hosts a test class over HTTP, invokes new ApoClassLoader(baseUrl, className).getMyClass(), and observes a constructor-created marker. This does not demonstrate reachability in the shipped game.

title: Working-directory class files execute before AI type checking
code_excerpt:
byte data[] = loadClassData(filename);
c = defineClass (name, data, 0, data.length);
entry_point: An untrusted local AI class under player/<binary-name>.class. Human and Easy are selected automatically at TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:64 and :82; alternatively, the user supplies the binary name through the dialog at :135-138.
sink: TutorVolleyClassLoader.java:43 calls defineClass on the file bytes, and TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:147 invokes Class.newInstance(). The cast to TutorVolleyAI does not occur until :148, after initialization and the constructor have executed.
data_path: TutorVolleyMain.main at TutorVolleyMain.java:96-98 constructs the window; its constructor calls TutorVolleyPanelOptions.setAI at :48. setAI calls loadPlayer at TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:64 or :82. loadPlayer creates TutorVolleyClassLoader with relative root "player" at :146. TutorVolleyClassLoader.loadClass maps the name to a filename at :38, opens it at :88 and :99, reads it at :103, and defines it at :43. Control returns to loadPlayer, which instantiates it at TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:147.
attack_scenario: An attacker distributes a malicious AI class as player/Human.class or replaces that file in a copied game directory. The victim launches TutorVolleyMain. Startup calls setAI before the window is made visible (TutorVolleyMain.java:48 and :61), so the file is defined and instantiated without another click. A static initializer or public no-argument constructor then runs arbitrary Java code with the victim's OS permissions. A custom class can instead be placed under player and selected using either Load Player button, whose handlers call loadPlayer at TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:236 and :257.
preconditions: The attacker must get a matching .class file into the process working directory's player subtree, for example by convincing the victim to install a downloaded AI. Automatic launch requires the binary name Human or Easy; manual loading requires the victim to select the matching name. No network delivery exists in this variant, and no privilege beyond the game process's user account is gained.
validation_plan: On a disposable runnable copy, compile a default-package Human class with a public no-argument constructor and a static initializer that writes a uniquely named marker file. Place it at player/Human.class and launch tutorVolley.TutorVolleyMain with that directory as the working directory. Creation of the marker before the options window appears proves the startup path. The probe need not implement TutorVolleyAI because TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:147 instantiates it before the cast at :148; implementing the interface avoids the subsequent ClassCastException.

title: AI class-file length directly controls heap allocation
entry_point: The length of the local player/Human.class or player/Easy.class loaded automatically at TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:64 and :82, or of a class selected through the Load Player dialog at :135-146.
sink: TutorVolleyClassLoader.java:96 allocates a byte array equal to the attacker-controlled file length, and :103 attempts to fill the entire allocation.
data_path: TutorVolleyMain.java:48 calls setAI; TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:64 calls loadPlayer for Human; :146 constructs the loader; TutorVolleyClassLoader.java:88 resolves player/Human.class; :93 casts File.length() to int; :96 allocates that many bytes; and :103 reads the entire file.
attack_scenario: An attacker supplies an oversized player/Human.class, such as a 256 MiB file, as purported AI content. Launching the game automatically attempts an equally large contiguous heap allocation before displaying the window.
